'''AO World plc''', [[trading as]] '''ao.com''', is an electrical retailer based in [[Bolton]], England. It operates in the United Kingdom (ao.com), and operated in Germany (ao.de) until July 2022 and in the Netherlands (ao.nl) until November 2019, specialising in household kitchen appliances, (such as washing machines, refrigerators, dishwashers and cookers) and other electricals.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.ao-world.com/about-ao/what-we-do/|title=What We Do|website=AO World|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-01-09}}</ref> It is listed on the [[London Stock Exchange]] and is a constituent of the [[FTSE 250 Index]].

==History==
The company was founded under the name ''Appliances Online'' by [[John Roberts (British businessman)|John Roberts]] in 2000. Prior to this, during a conversation in a [[Bolton]] pub, a close friend bet Roberts £1 that he could not set up his own company and disrupt the white goods market by selling appliances online.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/av/business-26628377|title=AO founder claims business started as £1 pub bet.|work=BBC News |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131213112532/http://www.drllimited.co.uk/our-story.php|archive-date=2013-12-13|url-status=live}}</ref>

As well as selling directly to consumers, the company also sold kitchen appliances on behalf of other retailers such as [[Next plc|Next]], [[House of Fraser]] and [[B&Q]]. In 2009 the company acquired the distribution business Expert Logistics, enabling end-to-end control of their operation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ertonline.co.uk/Default.aspx.LocID-05nnew2og.RefLocID-05n04600f.Lang-EN.htm |title=DRL acquires Expert Logistics |publisher=Ertonline.co.uk |date=22 July 2009 |access-date=24 June 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131028124926/http://ertonline.co.uk/Default.aspx.LocID-05nnew2og.RefLocID-05n04600f.Lang-EN.htm |archive-date=28 October 2013}}</ref>

In 2013 ''Appliances Online'' rebranded to ''AO.com'', which included a redesign of their logo to its current state.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.prolificnorth.co.uk/digital/featured/2013/09/appliances-online-looking-diversify-after-10-associates-rebrand|title=Appliances Online looking to diversify after 10 Associates rebrand|date=2 September 2013|website=Prolific North}}</ref>

In February 2014, the company was floated on the [[London Stock Exchange]] as AO World.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/2014-02-26/online-appliances-seller-ao-world-valued-at-2-billion-in-ipo.html|title=Online Retailer World Surges on London Trading Debut|publisher=Bloomberg|date=26 February 2014|access-date=24 June 2014}}</ref> The IPO allowed the company to raise funds for European expansion.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2014/feb/07/online-appliances-reatiler-ao-float-london-stock-exchange|title=Online appliances retailer AO to float on London Stock Exchange|last=Butler|first=Sarah|date=2014-02-07|work=The Guardian|access-date=2019-01-14|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

In 2015 AO.com announced plans for their second overseas website, AO.nl<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ecommercenews.eu/ao-com-will-launch-in-the-netherlands/|title=AO.com will launch in the Netherlands|date=2015-11-24|website=Ecommerce News|language=en-US|access-date=2019-01-14}}</ref> In the same year, a number of AO employees completed a Germany to Bolton bike ride to raise money for a new playground.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theboltonnews.co.uk/news/12958005.bolton-business-to-fund-70000-playground-for-ill-youngsters/|title=Bolton business to fund £70,000 playground for ill youngsters|work=The Bolton News|date=19 May 2015 |language=en|access-date=2019-01-14}}</ref>

In 2016 to support its European expansion, AO opened its {{convert|84000|sqm|adj=on}} headquarters in [[Bergheim, North Rhine-Westphalia|Bergheim]], Germany.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.prologis.com/build-to-suit/build-suit-ao-bergheim-germany|title=Build-to-Suit for AO in Bergheim, Germany|date=2017-03-13|website=Prologis|language=en|access-date=2019-01-14}}</ref> 

In 2017 the company announced it would sponsor the 11th series of [[ITV (TV channel)|ITV]] show, ''[[Britain's Got Talent]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.prolificnorth.co.uk/broadcasting/digital/2017/03/aocom-sponsor-britains-got-talent-after-mediacom-north-deal|title=AO.com to sponsor Britain's Got Talent after MediaCom North deal|date=2017-03-06|website=Prolific North|language=en|access-date=2019-01-14}}</ref> It also announced that it would extend its sponsorship with [[Lancashire County Cricket Club]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/business/business-news/aocom-extends-sponsorship-lancashire-county-12882455|title=AO.com extends sponsorship with Lancashire County Cricket Club|last=Begum|first=Shelina|date=2017-04-12|work=Manchester Evening News|access-date=2019-01-14}}</ref> It was also reported that company founder, Roberts, would step down as CEO, remaining on the board as founder and executive director. The former COO, Steve Caunce, took over as CEO.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ft.com/content/f1748180-f929-11e6-9516-2d969e0d3b65|title=AO World founder John Roberts steps down as CEO|website=Financial Times|date=22 February 2017 |language=en-GB|access-date=2019-01-14}}</ref> In March, the company announced that it had raised £50&nbsp;million through share placing to support plans for further growth.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2017/03/30/ao-world-raises-50m-share-placing-drive-growth-plans/|title=AO World raises £50m from share placing to drive growth plans|last=Bradshaw|first=Julia|date=2017-03-30|work=The Telegraph|access-date=2019-01-14|language=en-GB|issn=0307-1235}}</ref> The retailer also announced that it was to open a recycling plant in [[Telford]], Shropshire.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.letsrecycle.com/news/latest-news/ao-and-trg-merge-to-form-fridge-and-weee-recycling-giant/|title=AO and TRG merge to form fridge and WEEE recycling giant|website=letsrecycle.com|date=16 June 2017 |language=en|access-date=2019-01-14}}</ref>

In January 2018, the retailer reported that it had opened a new office in [[Manchester city centre]], which was to be home to the business's in-house multimedia, IT and sales teams.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/business/business-news/aocom-online-electrical-retailer-moves-14232619|title=AO.com the online electrical retailer moves into the city|last=Greer|first=Stuart|date=2018-02-01|work=Manchester Evening News|access-date=2019-01-14}}</ref> In April, the business announced that it had become one of only 20 businesses in the world to have received over 100,000 [[Trustpilot]] reviews.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.businesscloud.co.uk/news/aocom-reaches-100000-trustpilot-reviews|title=AO.com reaches 100,000 Trustpilot reviews|website=BusinessCloud.co.uk|language=en|access-date=2019-01-14}}</ref> In July, the business launched its new brand campaign, Delivering Tomorrow.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theboltonnews.co.uk/news/16367643.bolton-firm-ao-creates-new-hollywood-style-advert-to-save-the-sun/|title=Video: Bolton firm AO creates new Hollywood-style advert - to save the sun!|work=The Bolton News|date=20 July 2018 |language=en|access-date=2019-01-14}}</ref> It was also reported that it had committed to building a second major fridge recycling facility in the south east of England.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.letsrecycle.com/news/latest-news/ao-to-build-fridge-plant-in-south-east-england/|title=AO to build fridge plant in South East England|website=letsrecycle.com|date=17 July 2018 |language=en|access-date=2019-01-14}}</ref> The company also confirmed that it had completed the acquisition of the online phone retailer Mobile Phones Direct for £32.5&nbsp;million, as it looked to expand its offering in the mobile phone sector.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2018/11/ao-world-buy-mobile-phones-direct-32-5m/|title=AO World to buy Mobile Phones Direct for £32.5m|last=Stevens|first=Ben|date=2018-11-09|website=Retail Gazette|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-01-14}}</ref>

In January 2019, it was announced that Caunce would step down as CEO and Roberts would reassume the role.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-aoworld-chairman-idUKKCN1PP0Q4|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190131145501/https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-aoworld-chairman-idUKKCN1PP0Q4|url-status=dead|archive-date=31 January 2019|title=CEO of electricals retailer AO World to step down, founder to...|date=2019-01-31|work=Reuters|access-date=2019-01-31|language=en}}</ref>

AO's recycling plant in Telford processed its millionth fridge in July 2019.<ref>{{cite web|author=Robert Sant, AO Recycling |url=https://www.letsrecycle.com/news/latest-news/ao-recycling-million-fridges/ |title=AO hits millionth recycled fridge milestone |date=12 July 2019 |publisher=letsrecycle.com |access-date=2020-06-03}}</ref>

AO Mobile launched in August 2019, offering all UK mobile networks and all handset manufacturers. Roberts described the launch as "a game changer for mobile phone customers".<ref>{{cite web|author=George MacDonald |url=https://www.retail-week.com/electricals/ao-launches-game-changing-mobile-phone-business/7032621.article?authent=1 |title=AO launches 'game changing' mobile phone business &#124; News |publisher=Retail Week |date=2020-02-27 |access-date=2020-06-03}}</ref>

In August 2019, AO launched AO Finance in partnership with consumer finance provider [[NewDay (company)|NewDay]]. AO Finance offers a rolling credit facility that gives customers access to essential products through affordable finance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.yourmoney.com/credit-cards-loans/ao-launches-ao-finance-to-spread-the-cost-of-purchases/ |title=AO launches AO Finance to spread the cost of purchases - Your Money |publisher=Your Money|date=2019-09-19 |access-date=2020-08-13}}</ref>

In October 2019, AO's plastic plant was unveiled as the company announced its ambition to use its recycling capabilities to ultimately make new fridges from the recycled materials extracted from old ones.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/av/business-50594471 |title=Can old fridges be recycled to make new ones? |publisher=BBC News |date=2019-11-29 |access-date=2020-06-03}}</ref>

Announcing its interim financial results in November 2019, Roberts confirmed that AO would close its operation in the Netherlands to focus on its German business. Roberts explained that the team did not have the bandwidth to fix both markets but remained committed to future international expansion once the German model was proven.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ft.com/content/87e605fe-0aba-11ea-bb52-34c8d9dc6d84|title=AO World ditches Dutch arm to focus on UK and Germany|newspaper=Financial Times|date=19 November 2019 |access-date=3 June 2020}}</ref>

In April 2020, AO Business continued to grow and after only six months in the housebuilders sector, secured over 12,000 building plots.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.essentialretail.com/news/aocom-b2b-division-expands-team/ |title=AO.com B2B division expands team after quick growth - Essential Retail |publisher=Essential Retail |date=2020-04-20 |access-date=2020-08-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200715110701/https://www.essentialretail.com/news/aocom-b2b-division-expands-team/ |archive-date=15 July 2020 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Following a strategic review in July 2022, AO exited the housebuilder market to focus on [[business-to-business]] sectors that better fitted its model. This includes kitchen manufacturers and retailers, such as its partnership with [[Homebase]], which launched in January 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2022/08/ao-electricals-online/|title=AO.com plunges to full-year loss with further sales fall expected - Retail Gazette|first=Mark|last=Faithfull|date=18 August 2022|website=www.retailgazette.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kbbreview.com/50115/news/kitchen-showroom-retail-is-a-phenomenal-opportunity-says-ao-boss/|title=Kitchen showroom retail is a 'phenomenal opportunity' says AO boss|first=Vicki|last=Evans|date=18 October 2022|website=kbbreview}}</ref>

In September 2020, AO announced that it would be the new headline sponsor of [[Manchester Arena]]. The announcement came as operators ASM Global were submitting a planning application for phase one of its redevelopment. In a five-year deal, the rebranded AO Arena would see live events resuming once the [[2019-2020 COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19]]-related restrictions on venues were lifted.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/whats-on/whats-on-news/manchester-arenas-new-name-revealed-18864103 |title= Manchester Arena's new name revealed as bold redesign plans take another step forward|work=Manchester Evening News|date=2020-09-02 |access-date=2020-09-02}}</ref>

In October 2020, AO announced plans to open five 'stores-within-a-store' with [[Tesco]] as part of a six-month partnership trial with the supermarket.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/ao-electricals-middleton-store-jobs-19101445 |title= AO, let's go... to Middleton - electrical giant to open first ever store at Tesco Extra|publisher= Manchester Evening News|date=2020-10-14 |access-date=2020-10-16}}</ref> It ended the trial in July 2022.<ref>{{cite web |last=Goldfingle |first=Gemma |title=AO.com ditches Tesco concession trial - Retail Gazette |url=https://www.retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2022/07/ao-tesco-concession/ |website=Retail Gazette |access-date=1 November 2022 |date=19 July 2022}}</ref>

Following the launch of its Value Creation Plan in 2020, an all employee long-term incentive that rewards value creation, AO announced a restructuring of the plan in September 2022, which saw the scheme begin funding at a share price of £1.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chargedretail.co.uk/2022/08/25/ao-to-restructure-its-all-employee-value-creation-plan/|title=AO to restructure its all-employee Value Creation Plan -|first=Isabel|last=Cameron|date=25 August 2022}}</ref>

In June 2022, AO closed its German business, which accounted for around 10% of the group's revenue.<ref>{{cite web |title=AO World shutting German business to focus on UK market |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/business/ao-world-shutting-german-business-to-focus-on-uk-market-b2097224.html |website=The Independent |access-date=4 November 2022 |language=en |date=9 June 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Electrical retailer AO World swings to loss as costs mount and demand weakens |url=https://www.ft.com/content/8234ec00-3852-4efe-8e8f-354133287fd2 |website=Financial Times |access-date=4 November 2022 |date=18 August 2022}}</ref> The following month, AO successfully completed a planned £40&nbsp;million capital raise to strengthen its balance sheet and increase liquidity.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/fbb79082-2f37-4537-a4bf-3a463ed7e3e0|title=AO World plans £40mn capital raise after sharp share price fall|work=Financial Times |date=6 July 2022 |last=Alabi |first=Leke Oso}}</ref>

In Autumn 2022, AO appointed two new non-executive directors to its board. Former [[Pets at Home]] chief executive, Peter Pritchard, joined in September and [[Pret a Manger]] global chief digital officer Sarah Venning joined in November 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.prolificnorth.co.uk/news/appointments-and-recruitment-news/2022/09/former-pets-home-boss-joins-ao|title=Former Pets at Home boss joins AO|date=9 September 2022|website=Prolific North}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2022/11/ao-names-pret-a-mangers-sarah-venning/|title=AO names Pret A Manger global chief digital officer as non-executive director - Retail Gazette|first=Georgia|last=Wright|date=1 November 2022|website=Retail Gazette}}</ref>

At its half year financial results in November 2022, AO upgraded its full year profit expectations following its strategic pivot to focus on cash generation and profitability, which included reducing its cost base by £30&nbsp;million.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/68640d4f-70de-4f77-9559-47d6770978c3|title=AO upgrades outlook despite widening losses|work=Financial Times |date=22 November 2022 |last1=Provan |first1=Sarah |last2=Alim |first2=Arjun Neil}}</ref>

In the same month, AO announced it was the new headline sponsor of [[Manchester Thunder]], the current and four time Netball Super League champions.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://businessmanchester.co.uk/2022/11/07/ao-becomes-manchester-thunders-new-principal-sponsor-in-5-year-deal/|title=AO bolsters Manchester Thunder in new 5 year sports sponsorship deal|first=Sam|last=Allcock|date=7 November 2022}}</ref>

AO announced in October 2024 that it would acquire [[musicMagpie]], an online retailer that buys and sells refurbished electronics, for approximately £10&nbsp;million, as part of expanding the firm's consumer tech businesses.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/uks-ao-world-buy-musicmagpie-133-mln-deal-2024-10-02/ |title=UK's AO World to buy musicMagpie in $13.3 million deal |date=2 October 2024 |publisher=Reuters}}</ref>

In June 2026, AO.com exceeded one million reviews on Trustpilot with an overall average rating of 4.9 out of 5.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ao.com is rated "Excellent" with 4.9 / 5 on Trustpilot |url=https://www.trustpilot.com/review/www.ao.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260202093046/https://www.trustpilot.com/review/www.ao.com |archive-date=2026-02-02 |access-date=2026-06-22 |website=Trustpilot |language=en-US}}</ref>

AO Mobile, the company's [[mobile virtual network operator]] launched in August 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gray |first=James |date=2026-07-30 |title=AO Mobile introducing a new membership model to the UK mobile market |url=https://www.graystonestrategy.com/2026/07/30/ao-mobile-introducing-a-new-membership-model-to-the-uk-mobile-market/ |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=Graystone Strategy |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Operations==
[[File:AO Lieferfahrzeug.jpg|thumb|AO delivery vehicle]]
The company now occupies {{cvt|50,000|sqft}} offices and is based in [[Bolton]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bdaily.co.uk/articles/2013/08/08/fast-growing-drl-signs-deal-for-new-bolton-headquarters|title=Fast-growing DRL signs deal for new Bolton headquarters|website=Bdaily Business News|date=8 August 2013}}</ref> 

==Advertising==
The company launched a new advertising campaign on 3 May 2013 to mark the rebranding of the business from Appliances Online to ao.com. The first advert follows a fictional new employee called 'Dave' and his over-enthusiastic inductor on his first day at work. A further advert was aired showing 'Barry Catchpole'.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thedrum.com/news/2013/05/18/ad-day-appliances-online-barry|title=Ad of the Day: Appliances Online - 'Barry'|date=18 May 2013|publisher=The Drum|access-date=28 March 2016}}</ref> Its adverts feature a version of the [[Ramones]] song "[[Blitzkrieg Bop]]" in which the words "Hey! Ho! Let's go!" are reinterpreted as "A.O. Let's go!".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thetimes.com/business-money/companies/article/tempus-investors-look-at-ao-and-say-lets-go-z5jzkh89j55|title=Tempus: investors look at AO and say: let's go|date=3 June 2015 |author=Nic Fildes|work=[[The Times]]|access-date=16 July 2016}}</ref>

In May 2020, AO launched a new advertising campaign with an advert showing how Britain's homes were working harder than ever whilst many people were forced to stay home due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The advert demonstrated the hundreds of thousands of electricals AO have in stock ready for next day delivery across the UK.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SkH5vwMxP6w |title= AO.com TV advert - 1000s of electricals delivered safely|publisher=You Tube|date=2020-04-30 |access-date=2020-08-13}}</ref>

[[File:BSH Hausgeräte GmbH at Spree in Berlin 2024-06-16 01.jpg|thumb|BSH Hausgeräte GmbH]]

'''BSH Hausgeräte GmbH'''{{efn|name=pron1|{{IPA|de|beːʔɛsˈhaː ˈhaʊsɡəʁɛːtə ɡeːʔɛmbeːˈhaː}}}} ({{Langnf|de||BSH Home Appliances Company}}; stylized as B/S/H/) is a manufacturer of [[home appliance]]s in Europe. The group stemmed from a [[joint venture]] set up in May 1967 between [[Robert Bosch GmbH]] (Stuttgart) and [[Siemens|Siemens AG]] (Munich), and the company achieved annual sales of 15 billion euros in the year 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mishra |first=Urvashi |date=2026-03-26 |title=BSH clocks €15 billion revenue in 2025, bets on India premium push amid global slowdown |url=https://www.fortuneindia.com/business-news/bsh-clocks-15-billion-revenue-in-2025-bets-on-india-premium-push-amid-global-slowdown/131629 |access-date=2026-10-15 |website=Fortune India |language=en}}</ref> BSH is an [[acronym]] for {{Lang|de|Bosch und Siemens Hausgeräte}}.{{efn|name=pron2|{{IPA|de|ˈbɔʃ ʔʊnt ˈziːmɛns ˈhaʊsɡəʁɛːtə}}}} In September 2014, Robert Bosch GmbH agreed to purchase Siemens' 50% stake in the joint venture for 3 billion euros.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bosch To Buy Siemens' 50% Stake In BSH JV For About EUR 3 Bln |newspaper=RTT News |date=21 September 2014 |url=http://www.rttnews.com/2386805/bosch-to-buy-siemens-50-stake-in-bsh-jv-for-about-eur-3-bln.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140923104028/http://www.rttnews.com/2386805/bosch-to-buy-siemens-50-stake-in-bsh-jv-for-about-eur-3-bln.aspx |archive-date=2014-09-23 }}</ref> 

BSH is a global company with a presence in 50 countries. As of 2026, the company had 37 factories and a total workforce of about 56,000 people. The BSH product range includes large home appliances for cooking, [[dishwashing]], laundry (washing, drying and folding), refrigeration and freezing, as well as a multitude of small household appliances.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Inside BSH: Three Iconic Brands, One Home |url=https://gfu.de/en/gesellschafter/b-s-h/ |access-date=2026-10-15 |website=GFU Home & Consumer Tech |language=en-US}}</ref>

== History ==
BSH Hausgeräte GmbH (formerly Bosch-Siemens Hausgeräte GmbH – BSHG) was founded in 1967 as a joint venture between Bosch and Siemens and started out with three factories, that were all located in West Germany. In 1976, BSH acquired [[Pitsos]] in Athens, Greece (BSH Ikiakes Syskeveses A.B.E.). In the 1980s, recession and competition led to some companies in the industry merging, acquisitions and some going out of business. In 1982, BSH acquired the Neff premium brand, who were founded in [[Baden-Württemberg]], from [[AEG (German company)|AEG]] and established [[Constructa-Neff|Neff GmbH]].<ref name="Website-1">{{Cite web |title=BSH Bosch und Siemens Hausgerä {{!}} Encyclopedia.com |url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/books/politics-and-business-magazines/bsh-bosch-und-siemens-hausgera |access-date=2026-10-15 |website=www.encyclopedia.com}}</ref>

BSH developed new technologies and products, such as AquaStop for washing machines and dishwashers, which was patented in 1982 and introduced in 1985, a 90 cm wide oven in 1986 and a 45 cm wide dishwasher in 1987.<ref name="Website-1" /><ref name="Website-2">{{Cite web |title=History of BSH {{!}} BSH Hausgeräte GmbH |url=https://www.bsh-group.com/about-bsh/history-of-bsh/ |access-date=2026-10-15 |website=www.bsh-group.com |language=en}}</ref> In Spain in the years 1988/89, BSH acquired Balay in Zaragoza and purchased Safel in Pamplona.<ref name="Website-1" />

In 1993, BSH stopped using CFCs in refrigerator insulation. BSH made efforts to reduce the environmental impact of their products and became the first company to stop using [[HFCs]] in the majority of their refrigerators in 1994. The [[Montreal Protocol|Montreal agreement]] banned companies using [[CFCs]], from the end of 1995, with the chemical industry encouraging the use of [[HFCs]] as an alternative.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mackenzie |first=Debora |title=Fridge maker freezes out CFC substitute |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg14119110-300-fridge-maker-freezes-out-cfc-substitute/ |access-date=2022-07-22 |website=New Scientist |language=en-US|date=1994-02-05}}</ref>

During the 1990s BSH expanded further, they acquired [[Gaggenau Hausgeräte|Gaggenau]], they invested to take a controlling stake in Brazilian home appliance manufacturer Continental 2001 S.A. which provided them with six factories in Brazil and Mexico, they expanded into China via a joint venture with Wuxi Little Swan Group creating BSW Household Appliances Co., they obtained a majority interest in PEG Profilo Elektrikli Gereçler Sanayii A.Ş. in Istanbul, thus adding another production site to its portfolio in Çerkezköy, Turkey, and opened another factory in Nauen, Germany. They also agreed a further joint venture in China, which developed a factory in Chuzhou, and took a majority interest in the home appliance manufacturer Coldex, S.A. based in Lima, Peru. BSH also began to expand in the US, opening a factory in North Carolina and acquiring the California based Thermador Corporation.<ref name="Website-1" /> 

In October 2000, BSH agreed a joint venture with [[Hitachi]], with BSH taking a 60% stake and Hitachi having the remaining 40% stake, to create home appliances for the South-East Asian market.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Shimamura |first=Kazuhiro |date=2000-10-31 |title=Hitachi, BSH Create Joint Venture To Make, Sell Appliances in Asia - WSJ |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB972944939213684458 |access-date=2026-10-15 |work=Wall Street Journal |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660}}</ref> BSH also expanded further in the US by extending production facilities in 2003, for the Bosch range.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clagett |first=Leslie |date=2023-02-17 |title=BSH Home Appliances Celebrates 25 Years in North Carolina |url=https://kbbonline.com/business-people-news/bsh-home-appliances-celebrates-25-years-in-north-carolina/90608/ |access-date=2026-10-15 |website=Kitchen & Bath Business |language=en-US}}</ref> In the same year, BSH moved to a new group headquarters building in Munich, Germany.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-15 |title=KGAL and BSH finalise long-term lease agreement for Aviva office complex in Munich |url=https://cij.world/kgal-and-bsh-finalise-long-term-lease-agreement-for-aviva-office-complex-in-munich/ |access-date=2026-10-15 |website=CIJ.World |language=en-GB}}</ref> The company also continued to grow in China, building manufacturing facilities in Nanjing in 2004 and an appliance park in the region, with factories, in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Arend |first=Mark |date=2019-03-07 |title=Where Industries Climb the Value Chain |url=https://siteselection.com/where-industries-climb-the-value-chain/ |access-date=2026-10-15 |website=Site Selection Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

BSH Home Appliances Saudi Arabia LLC was founded in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia in 2010, as a joint venture.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ramkumar |first=K. S. |title=Saudi-German JV to sell eco-friendly home appliances |url=https://www.arabnews.com/archive/333757 |access-date=2026-10-15 |website=www.arabnews.com |language=en}}</ref> In 2011, the newly constructed BSH Technology Center, with research and office facilities, was opened in Berlin, Germany.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gewers Pudewill Technology Centre BSH Household Appliances, Berlin |url=https://www.gewers-pudewill.de/en/projekt/technology-centre-bsh-household-appliences/ |access-date=2026-10-15 |website=www.gewers-pudewill.de |language=en-GB}}</ref> In November 2012, BSH announced its intention to acquire the Polish home appliance manufacturer Zelmer.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cienski |first=Jan |date=2012-11-15 |title=Bosch-Siemens snaps up Zelmer |url=https://www.ft.com/content/501ee84e-7b1a-3197-86b9-316824a3d2d3 |access-date=2026-10-16 |work=Financial Times}}</ref> The transaction was completed in 2013.<ref>{{Cite news |title=In 2012, home appliance manufacturer BSH successfully endured the euro crisis. Significant increase in consolidated net profit |url=https://www.webwire.com/ViewPressRel.asp?aId=176356 |access-date=2026-10-16 |website=WebWire|date=2013-06-22}}</ref>

In 2014, BSH began to produce washing machines at its factory in Chennai, India.<ref>{{Cite news |last= |title=BSH Home Appliances to increase refrigerator production at Chennai plant |url=https://manufacturing.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/fmcg/bsh-home-appliances-to-increase-refrigerator-production-at-chennai-plant/111138648 |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=ETManufacturing |publisher=India Times |language=en}}</ref> Four years previously, the company had established a wholly owned subsidiary and offices in the country, prior to launching washing machines in 2011.<ref name="Website-3">{{Cite web |last=Srivastava |first=Gunjan |date=2015-12-07 |title=Bosch Siemens' made for India washing machines |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/my-learnings/bosch-siemens-made-for-india-washing-machines/41669/1 |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=www.forbesindia.com |language=en}}</ref> Other products such as refrigerators and dishwashers were also launched.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2011-09-21 |title=BSH Home introduces range of products |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/companies/bsh-home-introduces-range-of-products/article2473770.ece |access-date=2026-10-17 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> Prior to 2010, the company's products were sold via a distributor.<ref name="Website-3" />

On September 22, 2014, Siemens and Bosch announced that Siemens would be selling all its shares in their joint enterprise to Bosch, pending the approval of the antitrust authorities.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Alessi |first=Christopher |date=2014-09-22 |title=Siemens to Sell 50% Stake in Appliance Joint Venture to Bosch for $3.85 Billion |url=http://online.wsj.com/articles/siemens-to-sell-50-stake-in-appliance-joint-venture-to-bosch-for-3-85-billion-1411373379 |access-date=2026-10-17 |work=Wall Street Journal |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2014-09-22 |title=Siemens to sell stake in household appliances JV for 3 billion euro |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/business/siemens-to-sell-stake-in-household-appliances-jv-for-3-billion-euro-idUSKBN0HH01A/ |access-date=2026-10-17 |work=Reuters |language=en-US}}</ref> The sale was completed on January 5, 2015, after receiving competition authority approval, and from that point on the company was fully owned by Bosch. As part of the acquisition, the company's name was changed to BSH Hausgeräte GmbH.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wolf |first=Alan |date=2015-01-05 |title=Bosch Buys Siemens’ Stake In Majap Biz |url=https://www.twice.com/product/bosch-buys-siemens-stake-majap-biz-55468 |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=TWICE |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-01-15 |title=Bosch completes acquisition of Siemens' shares in BSH. |url=https://grandeconsumo.com/en/Bosch-completes-the-acquisition-of-Siemens-shares-in-BSH./ |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=Grande Consumo |language=en}}</ref>

In 2020, BSH sold the rights to its Zelmer brand to the Spanish group B&B Trends.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-01-14 |title=B&B Trends S.L. acquires the historic Zelmer brand from the BSH group |url=https://sdafactory.com/en/bb-trends-s-l-adquiere-la-historica-marca-zelmer-al-grupo-bsh/ |access-date=2022-07-26 |website=SDA Factory |language=en-EN}}</ref> It was reported in 2021, that [[Pyramis]] had acquired the Pitsos factory in Athens from BSH.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-05-25 |title=Long-time appliance maker Pitsos, a subsidiary of BSH, to remain in operation after purchase by Greece-based Pyramis |url=https://www.naftemporiki.gr/english/583133/long-time-appliance-maker-pitsos-a-subsidiary-of-bsh-to-remain-in-operation-after-purchase-by-greece-based-pyramis/ |access-date=2026-10-15 |website=www.naftemporiki.gr}}</ref> BSH business activities in Russia were impacted by the [[Russo-Ukrainian war]] and sanctions. In 2023 they sought to sell their St. Petersburg factory, but the plant was taken over by way of a [[presidential decree]] in 2024, and is now being run by a subsidiary of [[Gazprom]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-06-21 |title=Bosch subsidiary BSH: no decision yet on Russia business |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/bosch-subsidiary-bsh-no-decision-yet-russia-business-2023-06-21/ |access-date=2026-10-15 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Mihaylova |first=Olesya |date=2026-03-16 |title=Former Bosch plant, which the Germans didn't manage to sell, started producing Russian refrigerators |url=https://www1.ru/en/news/2026/03/16/byvsii-zavod-bosch-kotoryi-ne-uspeli-prodat-nemcy-nacal-vypuskat-rossiiskie-xolodilniki.html |access-date=2026-10-15 |website=www1.ru |language=en}}</ref> 

The business has opened showrooms that provide an immersive experience, in the US and Canada, where customers can also view and try products. The Houston showroom opened in 2024 and another opened in Beverly Hills, in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goode |first=Jo-Carolyn |date=2024-12-16 |title=BSH Home Appliances Opens Luxurious Experience Center in Houston: A New Hub for Innovation and Design |url=http://stylemagazine.com/news/2024/dec/16/bsh-home-appliances-opens-luxurious-experience-center-in-houston-a-new-hub-for-innovation-and-design/ |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=stylemagazine.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-18 |title=BSH Home Appliances Opens New Showroom in Beverly Hills |url=https://www.beverlyhillschamber.com/bsh-home-appliances-opens-new-showroom-in-beverly-hills/ |access-date=2026-10-27 |website=Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2025, BSH announced that they were building a new factory for small appliances in Rzeszów, Poland. The company have developed a significant presence in the country, over three decades, that includes multiple manufacturing sites, logistics and research and development facilities.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-30 |title=New giant factory for BSH in Poland |url=https://europaproperty.com/new-giant-factory-for-bsh-in-poland/ |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=EuropaProperty.com |language=en-GB}}</ref> In the same year, they announced that they would be closing two manufacturing plants in Germany, over the following couple of years.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wells |first=James |date=2025-10-16 |title=BSH issues statement on two German factory closures |url=https://www.applianceretailer.com.au/bsh-issues-statement-on-two-german-factory-closures/ |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=Appliance Retailer |language=en-US}}</ref> BSH Home Appliances Pvt. Ltd, which is the company's Indian subsidiary, has developed a large retail presence in the country, with 134 stores, as of 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-08-11 |title=BSH Home Appliances opens 30 Bosch Brand Stores across India in a single day |url=https://www.indiaretailing.com//bsh-home-appliances-opens-30-bosch-brand-stores-across-india-in-a-single-day |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=www.indiaretailing.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Notable innovations  ==
* 1985: BSH starts using AquaStop technology in washing machines,<ref name="Website-2" /> which prevents water damage from burst or detached hoses or hose leaks.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1985 |title=A new integrated safety system. Aqua-Stop prevents damages caused by water also from a burst water hose |url= |journal=Moderne Kueche |language=German |issn=0026-864X}}</ref>  
* 2002: BSH founds its first fully retractable patented SLIDE & HIDE oven door which creates space for convenient access to the inside of the oven.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Slide&Hide Backöfen von NEFF |url=https://www.kuechen-atlas.de/kuechenplanung/innovation/neff-slide-and-hide-backoefen/ |access-date=2022-07-22 |website=www.kuechen-atlas.de}}</ref>
* 2006: BSH introduces dishwashers with VarioSpeed technology which reduces running time for the same full performance.<ref name="Website-2" />
* 2008: BSH presents the first dishwasher with zeolite drying system which reduces the energy consumption of dishwashers by 20 percent.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Energy efficient dishwasher harnesses power of zeolites |url=https://www.theengineer.co.uk/content/in-depth/energy-efficient-dishwasher-harnesses-power-of-zeolites/ |access-date=2022-07-22 |website=The Engineer |language=en|date=2010-03-21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-29 |title=What Is A Zeolith Dishwasher? - (And Is It Any Good?) |url=https://kitchinsider.com/what-is-a-zeolith-dishwasher/ |access-date=2022-07-22 |website=Kitchinsider |language=en-GB}}</ref> The innovation has received awards for accelerating sustainable development.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Zeolith-Geschirrspüler der BSH weiter auf Erfolgskurs - Verbraucherportal Utopia zeichnet Umwelttechnologie aus |url=https://www.forum-csr.net/News/3862/Zeolith-Geschirrspueler-der-BSH-weiter-auf-Erfolgskurs.html |access-date=2022-07-22 |website=www.forum-csr.net |language=de}}</ref> It was awarded the "Innovation Prize for Climate and Environment" from Dr. Norbert Röttgen, German Federal Minister for the Environment, for promoting energy-efficiency products.<ref>{{Cite web |title=BSH Bosch and Siemens Home Appliances Group wins Climate Innovation Prize for energy-efficient products |url=https://www.albawaba.com/news/bsh-bosch-and-siemens-home-appliances-group-wins-climate-innovation-prize-energy-efficient-prod |access-date=2022-07-22 |website=Al Bawaba |language=en|date=2010-04-07}}</ref>
* 2010: BSH introduces the world's first washing machine with integrated dosing system i-DOS allowing accurate dosing of detergent. The system reduces water consumption.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Siemens launches iDos, the world's first washing machine with integrated dosing system |url=https://www.albawaba.com/siemens-launches-idos-world%E2%80%99s-first-washing-machine-integrated-dosing-system-379463 |access-date=2022-07-22 |website=Al Bawaba |language=en|date=2011-06-21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2010-08-09 |title=Siemens i-Dos washing machine |url=https://appliancist.com/laundry/washers_dryers/siemens-i-dos-washing-machine.html |access-date=2022-07-22 |website=Appliancist |language=en-US}}</ref>
* 2011: BSH launches its first full-surface induction with TFT touch display. The single large cooking surface with full-surface induction allows for pots and pans to be placed anywhere.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-02-13 |title=Gaggenau CX480 Full Surface Induction Cooktop {{!}} IndesignLive |url=https://www.indesignlive.com/products/article-1329086769 |access-date=2022-07-22 |website=Indesign Live: Interior Design and Architecture |language=en-US}}</ref>  
* 2021: The first ever portable fabric refresher FreshUp from BSH is launched that removes odours with plasma technology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=BOSCH Portable FRESHUP for Clothes {{!}} Parents News: Information For Families in the UK |url=https://www.parents-news.co.uk/national-news/bosch-portable-freshup-for-clothes/ |access-date=2022-07-22 |language=en-GB|last=McCarthy|first=Penny}}</ref>

'''Robert Bosch GmbH''' ({{IPAc-en|b|ɒ|ʃ}}; {{IPA|de|bɔʃ|lang|Robert Bosch GmbH.ogg}}), commonly known as '''Bosch''' (styled '''BOSCH'''), is a German [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[engineering]] and [[technology company]] headquartered in [[Gerlingen]], [[Baden-Württemberg]], Germany. It is 94 percent owned by the [[Robert Bosch Stiftung]], a charitable institution.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.bosch.com/company/ |title=Company overview |publisher=Bosch |date=31 December 2024 |access-date=23 December 2025}}</ref> Although the charity is funded by owning the vast majority of shares, it has no voting rights and is involved in health and social causes unrelated to Bosch's business.

The company was founded by [[Robert Bosch]] in [[Stuttgart]] in 1886.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.britannica.com/money/Bosch-GmbH |title=Bosch GmbH |publisher=Encyclopædia Britannica |date=23 December 2025 |access-date=23 December 2025}}</ref> In the late 1890s, Bosch started installing [[Ignition magneto|magneto ignition]] devices into [[automobile|vehicle]]s; the automotive sector would be a key long term market for the firm. In 1901, Bosch opened its first factory in Stuttgart. In 1917, it was reorganised as a [[corporation]]. Prior to the [[First World War]], the company generated 92 percent of its sales outside of Germany, however, Bosch lost most of its international holdings following the conflict. Using a combination of [[loan]]s and a greater focus on business acumen at the board level, the firm quickly rebuilt its international presence during the [[interwar period]], particularly in [[South America]] and [[Asia]]. Diversification efforts in the 1930s included the purchase of a gas appliances production facility, the development of an electric drill, electric refrigerator, and car radio.

Both prior and during the [[Second World War]], the company had links to the ruling [[Nazi Party]], using thousands of [[Forced labour under German rule during World War II|forced labourers]] in its production plants to produce ammunition and outfit [[Luftwaffe]] aircraft as part of the German war effort during the [[Second World War]]. Despite having to cooperate with the party, Robert Bosch formed a secret organisation that was focused on resistance to the Nazi Party, who were involved in a failed attempt to assassinate Hitler in 1944. At the end of WWII, all of Bosch's foreign assets were seized and most employees were laid off, however, the firm quickly recovered on the back of strong economic performance within [[West Germany]]. An economic downturn in 1966 motivated Bosch to adopt a strategy of decentralisation, diversification, and overseas expansion. The end of the [[Cold War]] led to the company expanding across the former [[Eastern Bloc]], setting up new manufacturing facilities and subsidiaries across Eastern Europe.

Bosch's core operating areas are spread across four business sectors: mobility (hardware and software), consumer goods (including [[BSH Hausgeräte|household appliances]] and power tools), industrial technology (including [[Bosch Rexroth|drive and control]]), and energy and building technology.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://assets.bosch.com/media/global/bosch_group/our_figures/pdf/bosch-today-2018.pdf |title=Bosch Today 2018 |date=22 May 2018 |work=Bosch Global |access-date=22 May 2018 |archive-date=23 May 2018 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20180523095844/https://assets.bosch.com/media/global/bosch_group/our_figures/pdf/bosch-today-2018.pdf |url-status=dead}}</ref> By the 21st century, Bosch had become the [[List of the largest automotive suppliers|largest automotive supplier]] in the world.<ref>{{Cite news |date=30 January 2026 |title=Top Auto Supplier Bosch Sees Tough Markets Persisting Until 2027 |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-01-30/top-auto-supplier-bosch-sees-tough-markets-persisting-until-2027 |access-date=31 March 2026 |work=Bloomberg News}}</ref> Due to this, the company's fiscal performance has often been impacted by trends impacting the automotive sector. In 2025, Bosch experienced a substantial drop in profitability that was attributed to a decline in global German car sales.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Autozulieferer: „Schmerzhaftes Jahr“ – Bosch-Chef verkündet Gewinneinbruch |trans-title = Automotive supplier: "Painful year" – Bosch CEO announces profit slump |url=https://www.handelsblatt.com/unternehmen/industrie/autozulieferer-schmerzhaftes-jahr-bosch-chef-verkuendet-gewinneinbruch/100195152.html |website=www.handelsblatt.com |date=30 January 2026 |access-date=30 January 2026 |language=de |first=Martin-W. |last=Buchenau}}</ref>

==History==
===1886–1920===
[[File:Robert Bosch mit Hut 1888 - 10031.jpg|thumb|upright|[[Robert Bosch]], founder of the company]]

The company began in Stuttgart-West as the ''{{lang|de|Werkstätte für Feinmechanik und Elektrotechnik|italic=no}}'' (Workshop for Precision Mechanics and Electrical Engineering) on 15 November 1886.<ref>{{cite book |last=Theiner |first=Peter |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=d0i9DwAAQBAJ |title=Robert Bosch: An Entrepreneur in an Age of Extremes |date=2019-10-15 |publisher=C.H. Beck |isbn=978-3-406-74146-3}}</ref> At the time of its founding, Stuttgart lacked municipal electricity, which hampered the business's early opportunities and pushed it near to [[bankruptcy]] before the local authority announced the decision to build a power station to serve the city in 1893.<ref name = "bosch crises">{{cite web |url = https://www.bosch.com/stories/bosch-during-crises/ |title = Crises throughout the company’s history |publisher = Bosch |access-date = 15 July 2026}}</ref> In 1897, Bosch started installing [[Ignition magneto|magneto ignition]] devices into [[automobile]]s, an early step towards becoming a key supplier of ignition systems over time. In 1902, the chief engineer at Bosch, [[Gottlob Honold]], unveiled the high-voltage magneto ignition system with a [[spark plug]].<ref>{{cite web |title=The beginnings 1886–1905 |url=https://www.bosch.com/stories/1886-1905-from-first-workshop-to-factory/ |department=Bosch Global |publisher=Robert Bosch |access-date=12 May 2019}}</ref>

In 1901, Bosch opened its first factory in Stuttgart.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bosch |url= https://www.companieshistory.com/bosch/ |access-date=25 October 2025 |website=CompaniesHistory.com}}</ref> In 1906, the company produced its 100,000th magneto. In the same year, Bosch introduced the eight-hour day for workers. In 1910, the Feuerbach plant was founded near Stuttgart, where Bosch began producing generators and headlights (Bosch-Light) in 1914. The motorization of road traffic led to the company's rapid growth after 1900. Bosch had a workforce of 45 in 1901, which expanded to more than 1,000 employees by 1908.<ref name="Bosch">{{cite book |last1=Bähr |first1=Johannes |url= http://dx.doi.org/10.17104/9783406683602 |title=Bosch |last2=Erker |first2=Paul |date=2015 |publisher=C.H. Beck |isbn=978-3-406-68360-2 |doi=10.17104/9783406683602}}</ref>

Bosch's international development began in 1898 with the opening of a branch in [[London]], followed the next year by outlets in [[Paris]], [[Vienna]], and [[Budapest]]. By 1909, Bosch was represented by trading partners on every continent. Bosch opened the first factory outside Germany in Paris in 1905 and the first on another continent in 1912 in Springfield, Massachusetts (USA). In 1913, Bosch founded an apprentice workshop to recruit young people for the production of automotive electrics.<ref name="Bosch" /> Prior to the [[First World War]], the company generated 92 percent of its sales outside of Germany.<ref name = "bosch crises"/>

In 1913, the company was subject to [[industrial action]] over employees being laid off as a result of a reduction in orders received.<ref name = "bosch crises"/> As the labour dispute escalated, Robert Bosch terminated all agreements between the company and [[trade union]]s and joined the metal industry employers’ association. The dispute was only healed by the [[First World War]].<ref name = "bosch crises"/> In 1917, Bosch was transformed into a corporation and remained so until 1937, when Robert Bosch regained sole ownership by purchasing back his shares. In the process, the company became a limited liability company (GmbH).<ref name="Bosch"/>

=== 1921–1945 ===
In the aftermath of the First World War, Bosch was compelled to forfeit the majority of its international holdings, including its US factories.<ref>{{cite web |url = https://time.com/archive/6746286/bosch-to-bosch/ |title = Bosch to Bosch |publisher = TIME |date = 17 November 1930 }}</ref> Thus, the company opted to rebuild its global activities throughout much of the [[interwar period]], which included expansion in both South America and Asia. In 1922, Illies & Company established a sales office for Bosch in Calcutta, India. In the years that followed, Bosch concluded contracts in Asia with sales partners in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia, as well as on the American continents with partners in Mexico, Peru, Colombia, and Ecuador.<ref name="Bosch"/>

In the 1920s, Bosch expanded its product range to include numerous automotive technology products essential for cars, such as electric horns (1921), windshield wipers (1926), and direction indicators ("trafficator", 1927).<ref name="Bosch" /> Robert Bosch personally led the project to develop a diesel injection pump, which went into production in late 1927.<ref name = "bosch crises"/> To fuel the company's expansion plans, [[loan]]s were taken out and the company's management board was restructured around business interests over technical ones.<ref name = "bosch crises"/>

Growth proved to be somewhat unsteady, occasional sharp short-term downturns in demand would sometimes necessitate drastic cuts; between September 1925 and September 1926, roughly 5,600 associates, almost half of Bosch's employees, were laid off. The company was deeply impacted by the [[Great Depression]], nessitating numerous lay offs, salary reductions, and the implementation of reduced working hours. Bosch pursued a strategy of diversification, which was achieved both through completing acquisitions and the launching of products into new markets.<ref name = "bosch crises"/>

Bosch purchased the gas appliances production facility from [[Junkers & Co]]. in 1932. In 1932, the company developed its first [[electric drill]] and presented its first [[car radio]]. In 1933, Bosch introduced its first [[refrigerator|electric refrigerator]] for private households.<ref name="Bosch" />

====During the Nazi regime====
Like most German businesses at the time, Bosch had links to the ruling [[Nazi Party]].<ref name="Heller1" /> Robert Bosch had commented on Hitler, after their first meeting in the early 1930s that "He wants to be a statesman and doesn't even know what justice is" and had to balance holding opposing views to the Nazi Party, whilst having to cooperate with them.<ref name="Website-1">{{Cite web |title=Der Bosch Kreis - EN |url=https://janglednerves.com/der-bosch-kreis-en |access-date=2026-10-28 |website=janglednerves.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Website-2">{{Cite web |title=Resistance to Hitler: The Bosch Circle |url=https://www.bosch.com/stories/resistance-to-hitler-bosch-circle/ |access-date=2026-10-28 |website=Bosch Global |language=en}}</ref> 

Prior to the [[Second World War]], Bosch under the direction of the Nazi Party began relocating armament production to Germany's interior. Bosch founded two factories in 1935 and 1937: Dreilinden Maschinenbau GmbH in [[Kleinmachnow]] and Feinmechanische Industrie GmbH (later Trillke-Werke GmbH) in [[Hildesheim]], for armament production. These factories were built secretly and in close cooperation with the Nazi authorities.<ref name="Heller1">{{cite web |url=https://www.translatetheweb.com/?from=&to=en&dl=en&ref=trb&a=https%253A%252F%252Fwww.stuttgarter-zeitung.de%252Finhalt.unternehmen-im-dritten-reich-robert-bosch-und-der-doppelte-spagat.dd553a40-57df-4ae8-a88d-3a46b7106081.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200131171817/https://www.translatetheweb.com/?from=&to=en&dl=en&ref=trb&a=https%253A%252F%252Fwww.stuttgarter-zeitung.de%252Finhalt.unternehmen-im-dritten-reich-robert-bosch-und-der-doppelte-spagat.dd553a40-57df-4ae8-a88d-3a46b7106081.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=31 January 2020 |title=Companies in the Third Reich: Robert Bosch and the double balancing act |last=Heller |first=Michael |date=12 January 2014 |website=stuttgarter-zeitung.de |publisher=Stuttgarter-Zeitung |access-date=31 January 2020 |quote=Many forced labourers worked at the Bosch plants. Bähr and Erker estimate the total number at 20,000 forced labourers, including 1,200 concentration camp inmates. At the end of 1944, the share of forced labourers in the workforce was around 33 percent; in the whole of German industry it was about 25 percent in August 1944. It cannot be said that the forced labourers at Bosch fared better than elsewhere. Especially in the factories far from Stuttgart, such as in Kleinmachnow near Berlin or in Langenbielau (Bielawa) in Silesia, there were attacks. 'The Russian workers and prisoners of war were subjected to arbitrary acts and denunciations contrary to all the principles of the company, and concentration camp prisoners were brutally abused at the Langenbielau plant,' the historians write.}}</ref> In 1937, Bosch AG became a limited liability company ([[Gesellschaft mit beschränkter Haftung|GmbH]]).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bosch {{!}} Science Museum Group Collection |url=https://collection.sciencemuseumgroup.org.uk/people/ap7762/bosch |access-date=25 October 2025 |website=collection.sciencemuseumgroup.org.uk |language=en}}</ref>

The Bosch subsidiary Dreilinden Maschinenbau GmbH (DLMG) in Kleinmachnow employed around 5,000 people, more than half of whom were [[Forced labour under German rule during World War II|forced labourers]], [[prisoners of war]], and female concentration camp prisoners, including many women from the [[Warsaw Uprising]].<ref>{{cite web |title=The Virtual Museum of the Holocaust and the Resistance – Irena Matusiak: Cookbooks and diaries |url= https://library.mcmaster.ca/archives/virtualmuseum/mod1-3.html |website=library.mcmaster.ca |access-date = 14 July 2026}}</ref> During the [[World War II|Second World War]], there were at least 3,000 workers in the mechanics division at the Bosch Hildesheim factory, almost all of them from nearby occupied countries; there were only 200 recorded German workers.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bergerson |first1=Andrew Stuart |title=Ordinary Germans in Extraordinary Times: The Nazi Revolution in Hildesheim |date=14 October 2004 |publisher=Indiana University Press |isbn=978-0-253-11123-4 |page=218 |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=rGTL30QmPhsC&pg=PA218}}</ref> In the last years of the conflict, all new German tanks included starter elements from the Bosch factory in Hildesheim; the company also had a monopoly position in the outfitting of [[Luftwaffe]] aircraft.<ref name="AIRSCIENCE">{{cite book |title=Air Science: Introduction to aviation |date=1953 |publisher=U.S. Air University, Air Force Reserve Officer Training Corps |location=Montgomery |page=48 |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=jJmlcqjKdNkC&pg=PA48 |quote=Even more poorly dispersed was aircraft magneto production, as the Bosch plant located at Stuttgart produced all the magnetos for the German military machine.}}</ref>

The company's cooperation with the ruling party was not without resistance. They formed a group known as the Bosch Kreis, which included Bosch executives, and were involved in resistance activities against the Nazi Party, including participation in a plan to assassinate Hitler, in July 1944, which was unsuccessful.<ref name="Website-1" /><ref name="Website-2" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=GDW-Berlin: Biographie |url=https://www.gdw-berlin.de/en/recess/biographies/index-of-persons/biographie/view-bio/robert-bosch/?no_cache=1 |access-date=2026-10-28 |website=www.gdw-berlin.de}}</ref>

===1946–1999===
At the end of the conflict, the company was compelled to stop production, causing nearly all of its workforce to lose their jobs, while all foreign assets were seized and foreign markets remained closed to Bosch for years.<ref name = "bosch crises"/> It opted to enter new markets during the 1950s, including mobile [[hydraulics]], medical electronics, and radio technology.<ref name = "newbus 1960"/> Between the late 1940s and the mid 1960s, the firm benefitted from strong economic performance within [[West Germany]]. Following an economic downturn in 1966, management sought to avoid layoffs by adopting a strategy of decentralisation, diversification, and overseas expansion.<ref name = "bosch crises"/><ref>{{cite report |last1=Puschmann |first1=Thomas |last2=Alt |first2=Rainer |title=Enterprise Application Integration: The Case of the Robert Bosch Group |publisher=Institute of Information Management, University of St. Gallen |year=2001 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/232615964_Enterprise_Application_Integration_-_The_Case_of_the_Robert_Bosch_Group }}</ref> The efforts included early work on research projects into emerging technologies, such as [[integrated circuits]], electronically controlled [[fuel injection]], and [[Anti-lock braking system|anti-lock braking systems]] (ABS).<ref>[8][19]</ref> This research led to a major milestone in 1978, when Bosch and [[Mercedes-Benz]] jointly introduced an electronically controlled anti-lock braking system, one of the first to reach series production, launching it in the [[Mercedes-Benz S-Class]].<ref>{{cite web |date=22 August 2018 |title=World premiere in 1978 in the Mercedes-Benz S-Class: Anti-lock braking system 40 years old |url=https://www.automotiveworld.com/?p=292727 |access-date=23 September 2026 |website=Automotive World}}</ref> In the 1980s, Bosch entered the telecommunications sector, producing technology for satellites and mobile phones.<ref>[18]</ref> In the 1980s, Bosch entered the [[telecommunications]] sector, producing technology for [[satellite]]s and [[mobile phones]].<ref name = "newbus 1960">{{cite web |url = https://www.bosch.com/stories/1960-1989-new-lines-of-business-and-electronics/ |title = New business 1960 - 1989 |publisher = Bosch |access-date = 15 July 2026}}</ref>

The company did not record a single operating loss throughout the [[Cold War]] era.<ref name = "bosch crises"/>The end of the Cold War and the fall of the [[Iron Curtain]] opened valuable opportunities to Bosch. By 1994, it had subsidiary companies across 13 countries of the former [[Eastern Bloc]]; the company also established manufacturing plants in the Czech Republic, Poland, Hungary, and the Russian Federation. In 1990, 49 percent of Bosch's sales were generated inside Germany, by 2000, 72 percent of sales came from outside Germany.<ref>{{cite web |url = https://www.clearygottlieb.com/-/media/files/directors-roundtable-world-recognition-of-distinguished-general-counsel-2019-pdf.pdf |title = Robert Bosch GmbH |publisher = WORLD RECOGNITION of DISTINGUISHED GENERAL COUNSEL |year = 2018 |page = 3}}</ref> Additionally, an early 1990s slump in the European automotive sector and an intense period of price-oriented competition against other suppliers negatively impacted Bosch. In response to lost orders, reduced working hours were enacted for 20,000 Germany-based associates, along with early retirement arrangements and termination agreements, which collectively involved around 13,000 employees.<ref name = "bosch crises"/>

===21st century===
In 2001, Bosch acquired ''Mannesmann Rexroth AG'', which they later renamed to ''[[Bosch Rexroth|Bosch Rexroth AG]]''.<ref>{{cite web |date=5 February 2003 |title=Changing of the guard at Bosch Rexroth Corp. |url= https://www.controleng.com/changing-of-the-guard-at-bosch-rexroth-corp/ |access-date=25 October 2025 |work=Control Engineering}}</ref> In the same year, the company opened a new testing center in Vaitoudden, close to [[Arjeplog]] in north Sweden. A new development center for automotive engineering, in [[Abstatt]], Germany was constructed shortly after.<ref>{{cite web |date=2002-08-05 |title=Germany: Bosch 'tops off' new R&D centre |url= https://www.just-auto.com/news/germany-bosch-tops-off-new-rd-centre/ |access-date=25 October 2025 |website=Just Auto |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2002, Bosch acquired Philips CSI, which at the time was manufacturing a broad range of professional communication and security products and systems including [[Closed-circuit television|CCTV]], congress, and public address systems.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.building.co.uk/philips-csi-sold-to-bosch/1020783.article |title=Philips CSI sold to Bosch |date=12 August 2002 |website=building.co.uk |access-date=23 December 2025}}</ref> In the 2000s the company developed the electric hydraulic brake, common rail fuel injection with piezo-injectors, digital car radio with a disc drive, and the cordless screwdriver with a [[lithium-ion battery]] in 2003. In 2004, Bosch bought Sigpack Systems from [[SIG Combibloc Group|SIG]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=100 years of innovation in the packaging industry |url=https://process-technology-online.com/top-news/news/100-years-of-innovation-in-the-packaging-industry/ |access-date=31 October 2025 |website=Process technology online - Konradin-Verlag Robert Kohlhammer |date=7 September 2006}}</ref>

Bosch received the {{lang|de|Deutsche Zukunftspreis}} ({{gloss |German Future Prize}}) from the German president in 2005 and 2008. A new development center was planned in 2008 in [[Renningen]]. In 2014, the first departments moved to the new center, while the remaining departments followed in 2015. In 2006, Bosch acquired [[Telex Communications]] and [[Electro-Voice]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bosch Acquires Telex Communications |url= https://www.assemblymag.com/articles/84431-bosch-acquires-telex-communications |access-date=25 October 2025 |website=assemblymag.com}}</ref> In 2009, Bosch invested about {{Euro|3.6{{nbsp}}[[1,000,000,000|billion]]|link=yes}} in research and development.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bosch registers most patents in company history |url= https://www.reliableplant.com/Read/12038/bosch-registers-most-patents-in-company-history |access-date=25 October 2025 |website=www.reliableplant.com |language=en}}</ref> Approximately 3,900 patents are published per year. In addition to increasing energy efficiency by employing renewable energies, the company plans to invest in new areas such as [[biomedical engineering]].

In July 2022, Bosch announced plans to invest {{Euro|3{{nbsp}}billion}} into its semiconductor chip production and [[research and development]] (R&D) over the next four years, including opening new facilities for manufacturing a computer chip development in [[Dresden]] and [[Reutlingen]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Wheatley |first=Mike |url=https://siliconangle.com/2022/07/14/germanys-bosch-invest-e3-billion-chip-manufacturing-research/ |title=Germany's Bosch to invest {{Euro|3{{nbsp}}billion}} in chip manufacturing and research |work=SiliconANGLE |publisher=SiliconANGLE Media |date=2022-07-14 |accessdate=2022-07-17}}</ref> China is both a market and a manufacturing location for Bosch. In 2023, Bosch had 58,000 employees in China and group sales of CNY 139.1 billion.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bosch (China) Investment Ltd. - MarkLines Automotive Industry Portal |url=https://www.marklines.com/en/top500/bosch-china-investment#:~:text=-In%202023,%20Bosch%20Group's%20sales,in%20China%20was%20nearly%2058,000. |access-date=26 October 2025 |website=www.marklines.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bosch Leverages Its China Innovations to Bolster Global Business, Country President Says |url=https://www.yicaiglobal.com/news/bosch-supports-its-global-business-with-china-made-products-and-tech-china-president-says |access-date=26 October 2025 |website=www.yicaiglobal.com |language=en}}</ref> In September 2023, Bosch acquired TSI Semiconductors, a [[Roseville, California|Roseville]]-headquartered [[silicon carbide]] (SiC) power device manufacturer.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Flaherty |first=Nick |date=2023-09-04 |title=Bosch completes acquisition of assets of TSI Semiconductors |url=https://www.eenewseurope.com/en/bosch-completes-acquisition-of-assets-of-tsi-semiconductors/ |access-date=4 September 2023 |website=eeNews Europe}}</ref>

Beginning in 2022, Bosch faced allegations of violating [[international sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine]] after Ukrainian authorities reported finding Bosch components in Russian military vehicles.<ref>{{Cite web |first1=Nik |last1=Martin |title=Bosch probed over Russia sanctions violations — report |url=https://www.dw.com/en/bosch-faces-probe-over-possible-russia-sanctions-violations-report/a-61173586 |work=[[Deutsche Welle]] |date=18 March 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/germany-probes-possible-exports-dual-use-goods-by-bosch-spiegel-2022-03-18/ |title=Germany probes possible exports of dual-use goods by Bosch – Spiegel | work=[[Reuters]] |date=18 March 2022}}</ref> Reports in 2024 have suggested that Bosch, along with other companies, have been selling appliances intended for the Ukrainian market in Russia.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bosch, Delonghi and Philips sell appliances made for Ukraine in Russia - Kommersant |url=https://mind.ua/en/news/20274263-bosch-delonghi-and-philips-sell-appliances-made-for-ukraine-in-russia-kommersant |access-date=5 December 2024 |website=Mind.ua}}</ref>

In August 2025, Bosch acquired the heating and air conditioning operations of [[Johnson Controls]] for {{USD|8{{nbsp}}billion}}.<ref>{{Cite press release | url=https://www.johnsoncontrols.com/media-center/news/press-releases/2025/08/01/johnson-controls-completes-sale-of-residential-and-light-commercial-hvac-business | title=Johnson Controls completes announced plans to cut 13,000 jobs at its auto parts business, representing 3 percent of its global workforce, in stages by 2030 as it relies more on [[artificial intelligence]].<ref>{{Cite news |
