==== Dishwasher ====
LG introduced its first dishwasher using an Inverter Direct Drive motor in North America in 2006<ref>{{Cite web |title=LG Motor Celebrates Its 60th Anniversary {{!}} LG Global Business |url=https://www.lg.com/global/business/insights/compressor-motor/blog/lg-motor-celebrates-60th-anniversary/ |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=LG Global |language=en-GLOBAL}}</ref> LG dishwashers are designed for automated cleaning of tableware and cookware and are typically sold as built-in kitchen appliances<ref>{{Cite web |last=Electronics |first=L. G. |title=LG Debuts Dishwasher With TrueSteam™, Virtually Eliminating Pre-washing for Greater Ease |url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/lg-debuts-dishwasher-with-truesteam-virtually-eliminating-pre-washing-for-greater-ease-137099758.html |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=www.prnewswire.com |language=en}}</ref> In 2022, LG introduced QuadWash Pro along with Dynamic Heat Dry technology, designed to improve drying performance through increased airflow and optimized heat circulation within the dishwasher tub.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brezinski |first=Mark |last2=Testing |first2=Senior Writer Who's Been |last3=Decade |first3=Reviewing Products for Over a |title=LG debuts dishwasher that promises better washing in less time |url=https://www.reviewed.com/dishwashers/news/lg-debuts-quadwash-pro-and-dynamic-heat-dry-dishwasher |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=Reviewed |language=en}}</ref> In 2023 several LG dishwasher models received the [[Energy Star|ENERGY STAR]] Most Efficient designation for meeting high energy- and water-efficiency standards.<ref>{{Cite web |last=USA |first=LG Electronics |title=LG DISHWASHERS EARN ENERGY STAR 'MOST EFFICIENT 2023' DESIGNATION |url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/lg-dishwashers-earn-energy-star-most-efficient-2023-designation-301737747.html |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=www.prnewswire.com |language=en}}</ref>

==== SKS ====
{{Main|SKS (brand)}}

In 2016, LG launched SKS (formerly Signature Kitchen Suite) as its luxury built-in appliance line, focused on the high-premium product tier. It launched first in the US at the 2016 [[National Kitchen & Bath Association|Kitchen & Bath Industry Show]] (KBIS) show.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kim |first=Chae-Yeon |date=February 20, 2025 |title=LG renames premium built-in appliance brand; Moody's outlook up - KED Global |url=https://www.kedglobal.com/electronics/newsView/ked202502200006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250902232849/https://www.kedglobal.com/electronics/newsView/ked202502200006 |archive-date=2025-09-02 |access-date=2025-11-03 |work=KED Global |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tintari |first=Maegan |date=February 29, 2016 |title=The NEW Signature Kitchen Suite Double Wall Oven I'm Lusting Over |url=https://lovemaegan.com/the-new-signature-kitchen-suite-double-wall-oven-im-lusting-over/ |access-date=2025-11-03 |website=lovemaegan.com}}</ref> In early 2019, LG opened an appliance [[showroom]] intended for [[architect]]s, designers and consumers, called the "Experience & Design Center," in [[Napa, California]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Quackenbush |first=Gary |date=2019-01-15 |title=$10M new Napa luxury kitchen appliance showroom beginning of LG Electronics |url=https://www.northbaybusinessjournal.com/article/industry-news/10m-new-napa-luxury-kitchen-appliance-showroom-beginning-of-lg-electronics/ |access-date=2025-11-03 |website=The Press Democrat |language=en-US}}</ref> In February 2025, LG formally abbreviated the brand name from "Signature Kitchen Suite" to "SKS," at KBIS in [[Las Vegas]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2025-03-14 |title=LG Formally Rebrands Signature Suite Line - YourSource News |url=https://yoursourcenews.com/2025/03/lg-formally-rebrands-signature-suite-line/ |access-date=2025-11-03 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Pibl |first=Chandler |title=The 12 Most Exciting Launches We Saw At KBIS 2025 |url=https://www.modernluxury.com/best-new-launches-kbis-2025/ |access-date=2025-11-03 |website=Modern Luxury |language=en-US}}</ref> LG also debuted new branding and products at the same show, including a "hidden" induction cooktop.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Waddoups |first=Ryan |date=2025-03-06 |title=9 Standout Moments from KBIS 2025 |url=https://galeriemagazine.com/kbis-2025-highlights/ |access-date=2025-11-03 |website=Galerie Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sofia |first=Nurin |date=2025-02-22 |title=LG unveils new SKS branding for luxury kitchen suite at KBIS 2025 |url=https://www.techedt.com/lg-unveils-new-sks-branding-for-luxury-kitchen-suite-at-kbis-2025 |access-date=2025-11-03 |website=Tech Edition |language=en-GB}}</ref>

SKS's portfolio includes professional ranges, rangetops, wall ovens, combination steam and [[convection oven]]s, column, French-door and under-counter refrigerators and dishwashers.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kramer |first=Scott |title=How LG Is Making Smart Appliances Even Smarter |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/scottkramer/2024/10/21/how-lg-is-making-smart-appliances-even-smarter/ |access-date=2025-11-05 |work=Forbes |language=en}}</ref> At KBIS 2018, SKS debuted pro ranges with a built-in [[sous vide]] module, which was an industry first, and then added the sous video module to more ranges in 2019 and 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-01-31 |title=Signature Kitchen Suite Unveils First 36-Inch Range With Built-In Sous Vide |url=https://www.probuilder.com/products/appliances/article/55199444/signature-kitchen-suite-unveils-first-36-inch-range-with-built-in-sous-vide |access-date=2025-11-05 |website=Pro Builder |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Serra |first=Susan |date=2018-03-01 |title=Kitchen Tech Trends: We're Not Far from "Alexa, Cook Me Dinner!" |url=https://design-milk.com/kitchen-tech-trends-were-not-far-from-alexa-cook-me-dinner/ |access-date=2025-11-05 |website=Design Milk |language=en}}</ref>

=== Televisions ===
{{See also|LG Display}}
LG has been a television manufacturer since the early development of South Korea's consumer electronics industry. Under its former brand GoldStar, the company produced South Korea's first domestically manufactured black-and-white television in 1966. The company later expanded into color television, large-screen displays, and digital broadcasting technologies.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=50 Years Of LG TV History - Black & White to OLED |url=https://www.lg.com/uk/lg-experience/lg-lab/tech-story-the-50-years-of-lg-tv-history-and-its-timeline/ |access-date=2026-05-06 |website=LG UK |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In 2004, LG introduced a 55-inch Full HD LCD television, which at the time was among the largest television displays available. In the same year, the company also unveiled a 71-inch Full HD plasma display television.<ref name=":5" /> LG Electronics introduced its first [[Internet TV]] in 2007, originally branded as "[[NetCast Entertainment Access|Net Cast Entertainment Access]]" devices. The LG SL9000 was one of several new Borderless [[HDTV]]'s advertised for release at [[IFA Berlin]] in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=LG SL8000, SL9000, LH9000 and LH9500: TVs without borders |url=https://www.cnet.com/tech/home-entertainment/lg-sl8000-sl9000-lh9000-and-lh9500-tvs-without-borders/ |access-date=2026-02-19 |website=CNET |language=en}}</ref> They later renamed the 2011 Internet televisions to "LG [[Smart TV]]" when more [[interactive television]] features were added, that enable the audience to receive information from the Internet while watching conventional TV programming along with the world's first 84-inch Ultra HD TV<ref name=":5" /><ref>{{cite web|title=LG's CES 2011 HD lineup: SmartTV platform, network Blu-ray players and HDTVs|url=https://www.engadget.com/2011-01-05-lgs-ces-2011-hd-lineup-smarttv-platform-network-blu-ray-playe.html|website=Engadget|date=2011-01-05|access-date=2026-04-12}}</ref>

In November 2013, a blogger discovered that some of LG's smart TVs silently collect filenames from attached USB storage devices and program viewing data, and transmit the information to LG's servers and LG-affiliated servers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://doctorbeet.blogspot.fr/2013/11/lg-smart-tvs-logging-usb-filenames-and.html|title=DoctorBeet's Blog: LG Smart TVs logging USB filenames and viewing info to LG servers|work=Doctorbeet.blogspot.fr|date=18 November 2013|access-date=9 December 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://arstechnica.com/security/2013/11/smart-tv-from-lg-phones-home-with-users-viewing-habits-usb-file-names/|title=Smart TVs from LG phones home with user's viewing habits, USB file names|last=Goodin|first=Dan|website=Ars Technica|date=19 November 2013|access-date=9 December 2013}}</ref> Shortly after this blog entry went live, LG disabled playback on its site of the video, explaining how its viewer analytics work, and closed the [[Brightcove]] account the video was hosted on.

In 2016, exclusively to India, Indian arm of South Korea's LG Electronics Inc started selling a TV that would repel [[mosquitoes]].<ref name="UltransonicTV">{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-lg-elec-mosquitotv-idUSKCN0Z30F2|title=LG Electronics sells mosquito repellant TV in India|last=Pak|first=Nataly|newspaper=[[Reuters]]|date=17 June 2016|access-date=21 June 2016|agency=Reuters}}</ref> It uses [[ultrasound|ultrasonic waves]] that are silent to humans but cause mosquitoes to fly away.<ref name="UltransonicTV" /> It was released on 16 June 2016. The technology was also used in air conditioners and washing machines.<ref name="UltransonicTV" /> The TV is aimed for lower-income consumers living in conditions that would make them susceptible to mosquitoes.<ref name="UltransonicTV" />

In 2018, it was reported that LG was planning to sell big-screen televisions that could be rolled up and retract automatically with the push of a button come 2019.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-12-18/lg-is-said-to-plan-selling-tvs-that-roll-up-like-posters-in-2019|title=LG Plans to Sell TVs That Roll Up Like Posters in 2019|work=[[Bloomberg News|Bloomberg]]|date=18 December 2018 |access-date=18 December 2018}}</ref>

==== OLED ====
LG Electronics launched the world's first 55-inch [[OLED TV]] in 2013<ref>{{Cite web |last=Joo-won |first=Chung |date=2013-01-02 |title=LG starts sales of world's first 55-inch OLED television |url=https://www.koreaherald.com/article/140 |access-date=2026-06-01 |website=The Korea Herald |language=en}}</ref> and 65-inch and 77-inch sizes in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://uk.news.yahoo.com/lgs-77-65-inch-curved-4k-ultra-hd-212800999.html#aGcFcrs|title=LG's 77- and 65-inch Curved 4K Ultra HD OLED TVs are coming to the UK|date=26 June 2014 |publisher=Pocket-lint|access-date=26 June 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://online.wsj.com/articles/at-lg-more-bendable-tvs-lie-straight-ahead-1401297785?KEYWORDS=lg&cb=logged0.009054038673639297|title=At LG, More Bendable TVs Lie Straight Ahead|work=[[The Wall Street Journal]]|date=28 May 2014|access-date=28 May 2014|last1=Lee|first1=Min-Jeong}}</ref> With these launches, LG became the first company to mass-produce large sized OLED TV panels. In August 2018 at IFA in Berlin, LG exhibited the first 8K OLED television.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Denison |first=Caleb |date=2018-08-29 |title=Up close with LG's 88-inch 8K OLED TV. Here's why it matters {{!}} Video |url=https://www.digitaltrends.com/home-theater/lg-88-inch-8k-oled-tv-introduced-ifa2018/ |access-date=2026-06-01 |website=Digital Trends |language=en-us}}</ref> In October 2020, LG launched the first rollable OLED television available for commercial purchase.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Byung-wook |first=Kim |date=2020-10-11 |title=LG Electronics unveils teaser of world's 1st rollable TV |url=https://www.koreaherald.com/article/2446194 |access-date=2026-06-01 |website=The Korea Herald |language=en}}</ref>

At CES 2026, LG announced its 2026 OLED range, featuring a picture technology called "Hyper Radiant Color".<ref name="techradar-ces">{{cite web |last=Griffin |first=Al |date=January 2026 |title=LG announces new OLED TVs at CES — brighter G6, the C6 splits in two, ultra-thin Wallpaper OLED |url=https://www.techradar.com/televisions/lg-announces-the-lg-oled-evo-g6-tv-at-ces-2026-20-percent-brighter-lower-reflections-and-the-worlds-first-with-4k-120hz-cloud-gaming |access-date=4 August 2026 |website=TechRadar}}</ref> In independent testing, the flagship G6 measured 3,004 nits of peak HDR brightness, compared with 2,268 nits for the preceding G5.<ref name="techradar-compare">{{cite web |last=Davidson |first=James |date=27 July 2026 |title=I tested LG's newest OLED TVs side-by-side, and as a certified TV calibrator, there's one clear winner for me |url=https://www.techradar.com/televisions/i-tested-lg-newest-oled-tvs-side-by-side-and-as-a-certified-tv-calibrator-theres-one-clear-winner-for-me |access-date=4 August 2026 |website=TechRadar}}</ref> Its anti-reflection screen was certified by Intertek as "Reflection Free Premium", with reflectance below 0.5 per cent.<ref name="techradar-ces" /> A reviewer found that the screen reduced reflections while preserving OLED black levels, but observed a green tint affecting skin tones on the G6 and B6E.<ref name="techradar-compare" /> In June 2026, LG Display said that its large-sized OLED panels were the first to receive Intertek's "Perfect Color/Brightness Accuracy up to 500 lux" certification. The test maintains a constant average picture level, meaning that its results are not directly comparable with conventional peak-brightness measurements.<ref name="forbes-ld">{{cite web |last=Archer |first=John |date=29 June 2026 |title=LG Display OLED Screens Achieve World-First 'Perfect Color/Brightness' Certification |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/johnarcher/2026/06/29/lg-display-oled-screen-achieves-world-first-perfect-colorbrightness-certification/ |access-date=4 August 2026 |website=Forbes}}</ref>

The range also included the OLED evo W6, which revived the flush-mount "Wallpaper" design that LG introduced in 2017 and discontinued in 2020.<ref name="nbc-w6">{{cite web |date=January 2026 |title=LG's absurdly thin Wallpaper TV is back, and it's gone wireless |url=https://www.notebookcheck.net/LG-s-absurdly-thin-Wallpaper-TV-is-back-and-it-s-gone-wireless.1196387.0.html |access-date=4 August 2026 |website=Notebookcheck}}</ref> Available in 77- and 83-inch sizes, the W6 has a nine-millimeter-class body and uses a separate Zero Connect box to transmit 4K video and audio wirelessly to the panel.<ref name="lg-w6">{{cite press release |title=LG Electronics Unveils the Wallpaper TV: The World's Thinnest, True Wireless OLED TV |date=5 January 2026 |publisher=LG Electronics |url=https://www.lg.com/global/newsroom/news/media-entertainment-solution/lg-electronics-unveils-the-wallpaper-tv-the-worlds-thinnest-true-wireless-oled-tv/ |access-date=4 August 2026}}</ref> LG markets the W6 as the world's first certified 4K 165&nbsp;Hz "True Wireless" television.<ref name="lg-w6" /> In 2023, the company had described the 97-inch M3 as the world's first wireless OLED television, with wireless video and audio transmission at up to 4K 120&nbsp;Hz.<ref name="lg-m3">{{cite press release |title=LG Launches World's First Wireless OLED TV |date=3 August 2023 |publisher=LG Electronics |url=https://www.lgnewsroom.com/2023/08/lg-launches-worlds-first-wireless-oled-tv/ |access-date=4 August 2026}}</ref> The term "wireless" refers to the audiovisual connection between the Zero Connect box and the screen: the W6 display still requires a power cable,<ref name="techradar-ces" /> while a reviewer noted that both the M3 screen and its Zero Connect box require mains power.<ref name="whathifi">{{cite web |date=2023 |title=The LG M3 wireless OLED TV is cool, but I'm not sure I really understand it |url=https://www.whathifi.com/features/the-lg-m3-wireless-oled-tv-is-cool-but-im-not-sure-i-really-understand-it |access-date=4 August 2026 |website=What Hi-Fi?}}</ref>

==== Micro RGB ====
Micro RGB (marketed as Micro RGB evo) is a line of LCD televisions produced by LG Electronics. LG introduced the line at the Consumer Electronics Show in January 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LG TVs at CES 2026: Stunning wallpaper set, glorious Micro RGB colors, and better Gallery Mode |url=https://www.engadget.com/home/home-theater/lg-tvs-at-ces-2026-a-stunning-wallpaper-set-glorious-micro-rgb-colors-and-better-gallery-mode-073739600.html |access-date=2026-05-21 |website=Engadget}}</ref> Intertek certified the LG Micro RGB evo as achieving "Triple 100 Percent Color Coverage", and TÜV Rheinland certified the line under its "High Purity RGB Spectrum Display" programme.<ref name="cetd-micro-rgb">{{cite web |title=LG unveils 2026 Micro and Mini RGB evo TVs with certified high-purity color performance |url=https://www.consumerelectronicstestdevelopment.com/content/news/lg-unveils-2026-micro-and-mini-rgb-evo-tvs-with-certified-high-purity-color-performance |website=Consumer Electronics Test & Development |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref>

==== QNED ====
[[QNED]] (Quantum Nano-Emitting Diode) is a line of LCD televisions produced by LG Electronics. LG announced its first QNED Mini LED LCD televisions in December 2020, ahead of their official presentation at CES 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 December 2020 |title=Official: LG to launch 8K & 4K "QNED" miniLED LCD TVs in 2021 |url=https://www.flatpanelshd.com/news.php?subaction=showfull&id=1609215405 |access-date=2026-05-07 |website=FlatpanelsHD |language=en}}</ref> The line combines quantum dot colour enhancement, LG's NanoCell technology and Mini LED backlighting. It was the first LG television line to combine quantum dot colour enhancement with Nanocell filtering, which is used to reduce dull or impure colours.<ref>{{Cite web |title=QNED vs QLED TVs: Which One Is Right for You? |url=https://www.cramptonandmoore.co.uk/advice-centre/tv-advice/qned-tvs/qned-vs-qled-tvs#ql2 |access-date=2026-05-07 |website=www.cramptonandmoore.co.uk}}</ref> The QNED line sits below LG's OLED television range and above its standard NanoCell models.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LG Begins Global Roll Out Of Its Debut 8K And 4K QNED TVs |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/johnarcher/2021/06/30/lg-begins-global-roll-out-of-its-debut-8k-and-4k-qned-tvs/ |access-date=2026-05-07 |website=Forbes}}</ref>

==== NANO 4K UHD ====
Nano 4K UHD, marketed under the NanoCell name since its introduction at IFA 2017, is a line of LCD televisions produced by LG Electronics.<ref>{{Cite web |last=sarah|date=2018-03-08|title=What is LG's Nano Cell Technology?|url=https://palomakiconsulting.com/what-is-lgs-nano-cell-technology/|access-date=2026-05-22|website=Palomaki Consulting|language=en-US}}</ref>

The line uses a layer of one-nanometer particles within the LCD panel to absorb light wavelengths that fall between the red and green colour filters; conventional colour filter arrays allow these wavelengths to pass through, causing colour bleed between adjacent subpixels. The AU Review described the result as "more accurate colour, specifically through narrowing red and green wavelengths for more purity," along with wider viewing angles than standard LCD panels.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Singh|first=Chris|date=2020-07-07|title=LG 65-inch NanoCell 91 Review: A near-perfect all-rounder|url=https://www.theaureview.com/technology/lg-65-inch-nanocell-91-review-a-near-perfect-all-rounder/|access-date=2026-05-22|website=The AU Review|language=en-AU}}</ref>

In 2020, LG's 8K NanoCell models were among the first LCD televisions to qualify for the Consumer Technology Association's 8K Ultra HD logo, which requires a minimum contrast modulation (CM) value of 50 percent; independent testing by Intertek recorded the NanoCell 8K's CM value at approximately 90 percent, well above the threshold.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cohen|first=Simon|date=2020-05-01|title=What is Real 8K TV? LG's approach to 8K fully explained|url=https://www.digitaltrends.com/home-theater/what-is-real-8k-tv/|access-date=2026-05-22|website=Digital Trends|language=en-us}}</ref>

LG positions the Nano 4K UHD line as the entry-level tier of its television range, below its QNED and OLED lines.<ref>{{Cite web |last=White|first=Andy|date=2024-12-03|title=LG TV model numbers: LG's latest OLED, QNED and NanoCell TVs explained|url=https://www.expertreviews.co.uk/technology/tvs-home-cinema/lg-tv-model-numbers-explained|access-date=2026-05-22|website=Expert Reviews|language=en-GB}}</ref>

==== webOS ====
{{See also|WebOS}}

As of 2014, LG is using [[webOS]] with a ribbon interface with some of its smart TVs. LG reported that in the first eight months after release, it had sold over 5 million webOS TVs.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2014/12/17/7413221/lg-webos-2-0|title=LG's webOS 2.0 TVs are coming to CES|date=17 December 2014|access-date=2 January 2015}}</ref>

LG manufactures remote control models that use [[Hillcrest Labs]]' Freespace technology to allow users to change channels using gestures<ref name="Stevens">{{Cite web|url=https://www.engadget.com/2010/08/26/hillcrest-labs-brings-lgs-magic-motion-remote-control-to-live//|title=Hillcrest Labs brings LG's Magic Motion remote to life, cheekily points out that Sony uses it, too.|last=Stevens|first=Tim|website=www.engadget.com|date=26 August 2010|access-date=2 September 2017|archive-date=22 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190322141049/https://www.engadget.com/2010/08/26/hillcrest-labs-brings-lgs-magic-motion-remote-control-to-live/}}</ref> and [[Dragon NaturallySpeaking]] technology for voice recognition.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.computeractive.co.uk/ca/news/2140928/dragon-brings-voice-control-smart-tvs-set-boxes|title=Dragon brings voice control to smart TVs and set-top boxes|last=Greek|first=Dinah|publisher=Computeractive|date=24 January 2012|access-date=22 June 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120310012100/http://www.computeractive.co.uk/ca/news/2140928/dragon-brings-voice-control-smart-tvs-set-boxes|archive-date=10 March 2012}}</ref>

In late 2023, LG committed to providing major webOS upgrades for televisions sold from 2024 onward, along with selected 2022 and 2023 models.<ref name="fphd-webos-commit">{{cite web |last=Larsen |first=Rasmus |title=LG commits to 4 years of webOS upgrades for TVs |url=https://www.flatpanelshd.com/news.php?id=1703737177&subaction=showfull |website=FlatpanelsHD |date=28 December 2023 |access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref><ref name="fphd-webos-renew">{{cite web |last=Larsen |first=Rasmus |title=LG details plans for webOS upgrade of 2022–2024 OLED, LCD TVs |url=https://www.flatpanelshd.com/news.php?id=1710868863&subaction=showfull |website=FlatpanelsHD |date=19 March 2024 |access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref> The initiative was subsequently introduced as the webOS Re:New program, under which eligible televisions receive up to four major version upgrades over five years.<ref name="fphd-webos-renew" /><ref name="techradar-webos-commit">{{cite web |last=Marshall |first=Carrie |title=LG promises to look after your webOS TV for years to come |url=https://www.techradar.com/televisions/lg-promises-to-look-after-your-webos-tv-for-years-to-come |website=TechRadar |date=28 December 2023 |access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref>

webOS 26, LG's television software for 2026, adds Voice ID for loading individual user profiles and AI Concierge for providing context-aware suggestions based on viewing activity.<ref name="ecoustics-qned">{{cite web |last=Silva |first=Robert |title=LG's 2026 QNED evo AI Mini LED TVs Go Big with Screen Sizes Up to 115 Inches |url=https://www.ecoustics.com/products/lg-qned-evo-tvs-2026/ |website=ecoustics |date=23 May 2026 |access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref> Google Gemini and Microsoft Copilot support voice-based questions and related-content searches, with some AI search capabilities requiring a subscription.<ref name="ces-multiai">{{cite web |title=Multi-AI architecture (LG webOS26) |url=https://www.ces.tech/ces-innovation-awards/2026/multi-ai-architecture-lg-webos26/ |website=CES Innovation Awards |publisher=Consumer Technology Association |year=2026 |access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref><ref name="ecoustics-qned" /> The platform also supports Home Hub, Matter, Apple AirPlay and Google Cast, as well as a generative AI image feature on supported models.<ref name="ecoustics-qned" /> LG applies a security system it markets as LG Shield, which uses encryption to protect user data and personalized services.<ref name="ecoustics-qned" />

Gallery+, introduced in August 2025, allows compatible televisions to display artwork and other images when not in use, and was compared with art-display services offered by Samsung and other manufacturers.<ref name="lg-gallery-launch">{{cite press release |title=LG Gallery+ Turns LG TVs Into Design Elements That Personalize Your Living Space |url=https://www.lg.com/global/newsroom/news/media-entertainment-solution/lg-gallery-turns-lg-tvs-into-design-elements-that-personalize-your-living-space/ |publisher=LG Electronics |date=25 August 2025 |access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref><ref name="fphd-gallery">{{cite web |last=Larsen |first=Rasmus |title=Gallery TV is LG's answer to Samsung The Frame |url=https://www.flatpanelshd.com/news.php?subaction=showfull&id=1767072297 |website=FlatpanelsHD |date=30 December 2025 |access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref> At launch, LG said the service offered more than 4,000 selected images, with a free light version available in more than 150 countries and a subscription version available in 23 countries. Users could also generate images through Google Gemini.<ref name="lg-gallery-launch" /> By May 2026, LG stated that the collection had expanded to more than 5,000 artworks.<ref name="cepro-art">{{cite web |last=Boever |first=Nick |title=LG Has an Entire Art TV Lineup Now |url=https://www.cepro.com/cep/lg-has-an-entire-art-tv-lineup-now/626877/ |website=CE Pro |date=19 May 2026 |access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref><ref name="lg-arttv">{{cite press release |title=LG Electronics Launches Art TV Lineup Where Design Shapes How Art Lives in the Space |url=https://www.lg.com/global/newsroom/news/media-entertainment-solution/lg-electronics-launches-art-tv-lineup-where-design-shapes-how-art-lives-in-the-space/ |publisher=LG Electronics |date=18 May 2026 |access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref>

=== Audio ===
Since December 2017, LG has co-developed its soundbars with British high-end audio manufacturer Meridian Audio, whose digital signal processing technologies are integrated into the company's premium models.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-01-12 |title=New LG Soundbar Boasts Meridian Tech and Atmos |url=https://www.soundandvision.com/content/new-lg-soundbar-boasts-meridian-tech-and-atmos |access-date=2026-05-21 |website=Sound & Vision |language=en}}</ref> In 2025, LG Electronics and musician will.i.am produced the xboom line of portable Bluetooth speakers and wireless earbuds.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hodge |first=Kyle |date=2025-01-07 |title=will.i.am Unveils New 'xboom' Speakers Enhanced With AI |url=https://www.billboard.com/culture/lifestyle/lg-xboom-by-will-i-am-speakers-announcement-ces-2025-1235870172/ |access-date=2026-05-21 |website=Billboard |language=en-US}}</ref>

At CES 2026, LG Electronics introduced LG Sound Suite, a Wi-Fi-based modular home audio system. Unveiled through a joint announcement by Dolby Laboratories and LG Electronics,<ref name="dolby-lg">{{cite web |title=Dolby and LG Unveil a New Era of Home Audio With the World's First Soundbar Audio System Powered by Dolby Atmos FlexConnect |url=https://news.dolby.com/en-WW/259049-dolby-and-lg-unveil-a-new-era-of-home-audio-with-the-world-s-first-soundbar-audio-system-powered-by-dolby-atmos-flexconnect/ |website=Dolby Newsroom |publisher=Dolby Laboratories |access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref> it is documented as the world's first soundbar-based audio system to feature Dolby Atmos FlexConnect, a technology that detects the positions of compatible wireless speakers to optimize audio for asymmetric room layouts.<ref name="dolby-flexconnect">{{cite web |title=Dolby Atmos FlexConnect |url=https://www.dolby.com/technologies/dolby-atmos/dolby-atmos-flexconnect/ |website=Dolby |publisher=Dolby Laboratories |access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref><ref name="forbes-flexconnect">{{cite web |last=Archer |first=John |title=LG Unveils World's First Soundbar System Powered by Dolby Atmos FlexConnect |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/johnarcher/2025/12/17/lg-unveils-worlds-first-soundbar-system-powered-by-dolby-atmos-flexconnect/ |website=Forbes |date=17 December 2025 |access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref> Designed as a highly scalable and modular ecosystem, it offers more than 50 customizable hardware configurations,<ref name="mk-soundsuite">{{cite web |url=https://www.mk.co.kr/news/business/11979827 |website=Maeil Business Newspaper |access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref> allowing users to expand their setup by integrating various wireless speakers and subwoofers according to their preferences. The system's flagship H7 soundbar supports LG's Sound Follow feature, which utilizes ultra-wideband (UWB) positioning to dynamically adjust the sound based on the location of the listener.<ref name="audioxpress-flexconnect">{{cite web |title=Dolby and LG Unveil the World's First Soundbar Audio System Powered by Dolby Atmos FlexConnect |url=https://audioxpress.com/news/dolby-and-lg-unveil-the-world-s-first-soundbar-audio-system-powered-by-dolby-atmos-flexconnect |website=audioXpress |access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref>

==== Laptops ====
LG Electronics produces the LG gram, a line of laptop computers first released in South Korea in 2014 and expanded to international markets in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fingas |first=Jon |date=2015-09-28 |title=LG's lightweight Gram laptops arrive in the US |url=https://www.engadget.com/2015-09-28-lg-gram-laptops-come-to-us.html |access-date=2026-05-19 |website=Engadget |language=en-US}}</ref> The line focuses on minimizing weight, with some configurations weighing as little as 980 grams.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weigand |first=Matthew |title=LG Unveils 980g Ultralight Notebook, the Gram |url=https://www.businesskorea.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=2804}}</ref> It has expanded to include standard clamshell, convertible 2-in-1, and ultraslim configurations.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Devine |first=Richard |date=2018-12-13 |title=LG details two new gram laptops heading to CES 2019 |url=https://www.windowscentral.com/lg-details-two-new-gram-laptops-heading-ces-2019 |access-date=2026-05-19 |website=Windows Central |language=en}}</ref> In 2019, the gram line received three Guinness World Records for the lightest laptop in its screen-size category.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yonhap |date=2019-01-17 |title=LG's 17-inch laptop sets new Guinness World Record |url=https://www.koreaherald.com/article/1895679 |access-date=2026-05-19 |website=The Korea Herald |language=en}}</ref>

Beginning with its 2026 lineup, LG introduced Aerominum, an aluminium-magnesium alloy developed by the company, which LG said reduced weight while improving structural strength and scratch resistance.<ref name="verge-aerominum">{{cite web |last=Weatherbed |first=Jess |title=LG announces the 'world's lightest 17-inch RTX laptop' |url=https://www.theverge.com/news/852628/lg-gram-pro-17-16-laptop-2026-ces |website=The Verge |date=2 January 2026 |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref><ref name="lg-aerominum">{{cite press release |title=LG Electronics Introduces 2026 LG gram Lineup Elevated by Aerominum |url=https://www.lg.com/global/newsroom/news/media-entertainment-solution/lg-electronics-introduces-2026-lg-gram-lineup-elevated-by-aerominum/ |publisher=LG Electronics |date=2 January 2026 |access-date=27 August 2026}}</ref>

=== Heating and cooling ===
LG Electronics has developed heating and cooling systems since the late 20th century.{{citation needed|date=April 2026}} Its portfolio includes air conditioners, heat pumps, chillers, and building energy management systems for residential, commercial, and industrial applications.

==== Air conditioners ====
LG's air conditioning business dates to 1968, when its predecessor GoldStar introduced the GA-111, described as the first domestically produced air conditioner in South Korea.<ref>{{Cite web |title=디자인맵 {{!}} DESIGNMAP |url=https://www.designmap.or.kr/dt/DtDfFrD.jsp?p=71 |access-date=2026-04-21 |website=www.designmap.or.kr}}</ref>

In 1979, LG introduced the GA-100SP, described as South Korea's first wall-mounted air conditioner.<ref>{{Cite web |last=zoohihi@busan.com |first=김주희 부산닷컴 기자 |script-title=ko:45년간 현역으로 활동한 '금성' 에어컨, 고장 없이 LG전자 복귀 |url=https://www.busan.com/view/busan/view.php?code=2023070315432273171 |access-date=2026-04-21 |website=부산일보 |language=ko}}</ref>

==== Heat pumps ====
LG produces air-to-water [[heat pump]] systems for residential applications under the Therma V name.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HVAC - Air to Water Heat Pumps {{!}} LG Global Business |url=https://www.lg.com/global/business/hvac/residential-solutions/air-to-water-heat-pumps/ |access-date=2026-06-05 |website=LG Global |language=en-GLOBAL}}</ref> The company also produces heat pump [[chiller]]s for commercial applications.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LG Introduces Inverter Heat Pump Chiller {{!}} ashrae.org |url=https://www.ashrae.org/news/ahr-today/lg-introduces-inverter-heat-pump-chiller |access-date=2026-06-05 |website=www.ashrae.org}}</ref> The company entered the commercial chiller market in 2011 through the acquisition of a chiller business from [[LS Mtron]], a South Korean industrial manufacturer.<ref name=":8">{{Cite news |last=Global |first=KED |title=LG Electronics rises to global prominence in HVAC segment, ranks fifth - KED Global |url=https://www.kedglobal.com/electronics/newsView/ked202411200005 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260305114243/https://www.kedglobal.com/electronics/newsView/ked202411200005 |archive-date=2026-03-05 |access-date=2026-06-05 |work=KED Global |language=en-US}}</ref> In June 2025, LG agreed to acquire OSO, a Norway-based water heating manufacturer founded in 1932, with production facilities in Norway and Sweden.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Global |first=KED |title=LG Electronics acquires Norway's OSO in bold HVAC expansion - KED Global |url=https://www.kedglobal.com/mergers-acquisitions/newsView/ked202506300009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251207195145/https://www.kedglobal.com/mergers-acquisitions/newsView/ked202506300009 |archive-date=2025-12-07 |access-date=2026-06-05 |work=KED Global |language=en-US}}</ref>

==== HVAC systems ====
[[File:LG Multi V.png|right|204x204px|Multi V outdoor units]]
LG produces [[variable refrigerant flow]] (VRF) systems for commercial buildings under the [[LG Multi V Series|Multi V]] brand name, first introduced in 2006.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LG launches new VRF system |url=https://modbs.co.uk/news/fullstory.php/aid/16576/LG_launches_new_VRF_system.html|access-date=2026-08-10}}</ref> The fourth-generation Multi V IV was introduced in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Everitt |first=Neil |date=2013-11-06 |title=LG launches Multi V lV VRF |url=https://www.coolingpost.com/products/lg-launches-multi-v-lv-vrf/ |access-date=2026-10-18 |website=Cooling Post |language=en-GB}}</ref> The fifth-generation Multi V 5 followed in 2017.<ref>{{Cite news |title=LG launches new VRF system - Modern Building Services |url=https://modbs.co.uk/news/archivestory.php/aid/16576/LG_launches_new_VRF_system.html |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20261010005115/https://modbs.co.uk/news/archivestory.php/aid/16576/LG_launches_new_VRF_system.html |archive-date=2026-10-10 |access-date=2026-10-18 |language=en}}</ref> In 2023, LG announced the Multi V i, a VRF system featuring artificial intelligence that adjusts heating and cooling output based on the number of people in a room, humidity, and indoor and outdoor temperatures.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Everitt |first=Neil |date=2023-02-08 |title=LG's new Multi V i VRF is driven by AI |url=https://www.coolingpost.com/products/lgs-new-multi-v-i-vrf-is-driven-by-ai/ |access-date=2026-10-18 |website=Cooling Post |language=en-GB}}</ref> The company also produces large-scale chillers for commercial and industrial buildings, entering the chiller market in 2011 through the acquisition of a chiller business from LS Mtron, a South Korean industrial manufacturer. In 2017, LG began mass production of large-scale chillers using oil-free magnetic bearing [[compressor]] technology.<ref name=":8" /> In 2023, LG Electronics had received the Air-Conditioning, Heating and Refrigeration Institute (AHRI) Performance Award for the sixth consecutive year, across multiple product categories including VRF systems and chillers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LG Earns AHRI Performance Award for the Sixth Consecutive Year {{!}} ACHR News |url=https://www.achrnews.com/articles/152747-lg-earns-ahri-performance-award-for-the-sixth-consecutive-year |access-date=2026-06-05 |website=www.achrnews.com |language=en}}</ref> By late 2024, LG ranked fifth in the global large-scale chiller market.<ref name=":8" /> In December 2024, LG partnered with South Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy to expand exports of its chiller systems for data centers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ye-eun |first=Jie |date=2024-12-02 |title=LG makes big push to export chillers for AI data centers |url=https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10012134 |access-date=2026-06-05 |website=The Korea Herald |language=en}}</ref>

===Mobility===
The company launched a vehicle component division in 2013 and expanded it to cover in-vehicle [[infotainment]] (IVI) technologies, including audio, video and navigation, displays, telematics, and Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) vision systems, as well as EV powertrain solutions.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Global |first=KED |title=LG Group's received orders for auto parts close to $393 billion - KED Global |url=https://www.kedglobal.com/automobiles/newsView/ked202212280022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230202012912/https://www.kedglobal.com/automobiles/newsView/ked202212280022 |archive-date=2023-02-02 |access-date=2026-06-07 |work=KED Global |language=en-US}}</ref>

LG expanded its mobility component business in the 2010s through electric vehicle and lighting-related projects. In 2015, LG developed in-vehicle experience solutions for General Motors’ Chevrolet Bolt EV, investing more than $250 million in an engineering and manufacturing facility in [[Incheon]] for the project.<ref>{{Cite web |title=GM, LG partnership on Chevy Bolt may be roadmap for future deals |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/technology/gm-lg-partnership-on-chevy-bolt-may-be-roadmap-for-future-deals-idUSKCN0SE233/|access-date=2026-08-10}}</ref> In 2018, LG acquired ZKW Group, an Austrian automotive lighting company, for about $1.3 billion.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LG Elec, LG Corp buy Austrian auto light maker ZKW for 13 billion |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/world/europe/lg-elec-lg-corp-buy-austrian-auto-light-maker-zkw-for-13-billion-idUSKBN1HX0QB/|access-date=2026-08-10}}</ref> ZKW's customers include European automakers such as [[Volkswagen]], [[Audi]], [[BMW]], [[Porsche]] and [[Mercedes-Benz]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Customers |url=https://zkw-group.com/en/home/partners/customers/ |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=ZKW Group – BRIGHT MINDS, BRIGHT LIGHTS. |language=en-US}}</ref>

The company later expanded into electric vehicle powertrain components. In July 2021, LG and Canadian automotive supplier [[Magna International]] established LG Magna e-Powertrain, a joint venture manufacturing e-drive systems including e-motors, inverters, onboard chargers, and integrated power generation modules.<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |date=2020-12-23 |title=LG and Magna announce billion dollar joint venture in electric car gear |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2020/12/23/lg-and-magna-announce-billion-dollar-joint-venture-in-electric-car-gear.html |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref> Magna held a 49 percent stake in the venture, valued at approximately USD 1 billion, with LG retaining the remaining 51 percent.<ref name=":9" /> That same year, LG acquired Cybellum to enhance its cybersecurity capabilities in response to rapid electrification trends in the automotive market.

In 2021, LG developed an [[Android (operating system)|Android]] Automotive-based in-vehicle infotainment system with [[Renault]], which debuted in the Renault Mégane E-Tech Electric.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Schoon |first=Ben |date=2021-11-02 |title=LG shows off its take on Android Automotive, coming to 2022 Renault Mégane EV |url=https://9to5google.com/2021/11/02/lg-android-automotive-renault/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231201033552/https://9to5google.com/2021/11/02/lg-android-automotive-renault/ |archive-date=2023-12-01 |access-date=2026-06-23 |work=9to5Google |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2023, [[Hyundai Motor Group]] and LG announced—as part of their software-defined vehicle (SDV) solutions— the integration of LG’s [[webOS]] for Automotive Content Platform (ACP) in [[Genesis Motor|Genesis]] vehicles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bhushan |first=Bharat |date=2024-01-03 |title=LG Bon Voyage Trailer is Feature-Laden as Tiny House on Wheels |url=https://www.homecrux.com/lg-bon-voyage-trailer/229172/ |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=Homecrux |language=en-US}}</ref>

Additionally, LG manufactures advanced mobility solutions for numerous global automakers, including [[Volkswagen]], [[Renault]], [[Jaguar Cars|Jaguar]], [[Land Rover]], [[General Motors]], [[Toyota]], and [[Hyundai]]. The company also produces teardrop trailers<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lg.com/global/ces2024-lglabs/ |title=LG Labs |website=LG |access-date=5 February 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.homecrux.com/lg-bon-voyage-trailer/229172/ |title=New LG Bon Voyage Trailer is Feature-Packed as Tiny House on Wheels |last=Sharma |first=Bharat |date=10 January 2024 |website=Homecrux |access-date=5 February 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.homecrux.com/interview-sung-gul-hwang-lg-design-head/232693/ |title=Sung-Gul Hwang: The Man Designing LG's Future as it Extends Technology Beyond Homes |last=Sharma |first=Atish |date=5 February 2024 |website=Homecrux |access-date=5 February 2024}}</ref> and supplies displays for various other vehicle manufacturers.<ref name="LG supplies Genesis"/>

==== Head Unit ====
In-Vehicle Infotainment (IVI) systems are a core component of the digital cockpit, delivering integrated driving information and entertainment features to both drivers and passengers. LG Electronics has described the automobile as a "Living Space on Wheels" and develops IVI systems based on its experience in customer experience (CX) technologies.<ref>{{Cite web |last=www.etnews.com |date=2026-05-25 |title=LG전자-구글, 車 OS 협력 확대…단일칩으로 5개 디스플레이 제어 |url=https://m.etnews.com/20260522000248?SNS=00002 |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=미래를 보는 신문 - 전자신문 |language=ko}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=LG Brings 'Living Space on Wheels' Vision to Life With LG AlphaWare for SDVs |url=https://www.lg.com/global/newsroom/b2b/product-and-solutions/lg-brings-living-space-on-wheels-vision-to-life-with-lg-alphaware-for-sdvs/ |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=LG Global |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==== Automotive Display ====
To address the 'Screenification' trend where vehicles evolve into living spaces powered by diverse new form-factors with display technologies, LG Electronics and Mercedes-Benz have developed OLED-based IVI system for the Mercedes-Benz EQS, featuring a curved panoramic display that spans the entire dashboard.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Global |first=KED |title=2022 Mercedes EQS EV comes with LG's flexible OLED - KED Global |url=https://www.kedglobal.com/automobiles/newsView/ked202201130001 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241212144340/https://www.kedglobal.com/automobiles/newsView/ked202201130001 |archive-date=2024-12-12 |access-date=2026-08-06 |work=KED Global |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Consumer Electronics">{{Cite web |title=Consumer Electronics |url=https://www.lg.com/global/ |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=LG Global |language=en-GLOBAL}}</ref>

==== Telematics ====
Telematics, a portmanteau of telecommunications and informatics, refers to systems that connect vehicles to external networks to enable a wide array of services. LG Electronics leads the global market in this sector with world-class technology. LG firmly secures the top spot in the global Telematics Control Unit (TCU) market, with market research firm Strategy Analytics estimating its 2024 market share at 24.4%.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Counterpoint |first=Team |date=2025-04-07 |title=Global TCU Sales Up 8% YoY in 2024; LG Continues to Lead |url=https://counterpointresearch.com/en/insights/global-tcu-sales-up-8-yoy-in-2024-lg-continues-to-lead |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=Counterpoint Research |language=en}}</ref>

==== ADAS Vision System ====
Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS)—often called the 'eyes of the autonomous vehicle'—utilize cameras and sensors to perceive surroundings, detect hazards, and assist driver safety. In 2021, LG Electronics supplied the Mercedes-Benz C-Class with comprehensive ADAS camera solutions, including external front-facing cameras and in-cabin sensing technologies.<ref name="Consumer Electronics"/><ref>{{Cite web |date=6 October 2021 |title=LG전자 '자동차의 눈' ADAS 전방카메라 벤츠 C클래스에 공급 |url=https://news.einfomax.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=4170268 |access-date=6 August 2026 |website=news.einfomax.co.kr}}</ref>

==== Software ====
As the automotive industry shifts from hardware-centric designs to Software-Defined Vehicles (SDVs), LG Electronics has launched 'LG αWare,' its integrated software solution brand, positioning itself as a core player in the SDV era.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-11 |title=LG전자, SDV 솔루션 'LG 알파웨어'로 모빌리티 승부수...현대차·폭스바겐 협업 |url=https://www.theguru.co.kr/news/article.html?no=73950 |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=www.theguru.co.kr |language=ko}}</ref>

=== Mobile devices ===
In April 2021, LG officially confirmed that it will shut down its mobile division.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2021/4/4/22346084/lg-exits-smartphone-business|title = LG is quitting the smartphone business|date = 4 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/technology/news/story/lg-closes-down-mobile-phone-business-here-is-what-will-happen-to-existing-lg-phone-users-1787177-2021-04-05|title = LG closes down mobile phone business, here is what will happen to existing LG phone users| date=5 April 2021 }}</ref> Earlier, there had been rumours that LG considered selling its mobile division with [[Vingroup]] and [[Volkswagen Group|Volkswagen]] named as potential buyers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.androidpolice.com/2021/03/22/nobody-wants-to-buy-lgs-phone-business/|title = Nobody wants to buy LG's phone business|date = 22 March 2021|access-date=2026-08-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gsmarena.com/report_lg_considers_shutting_down_mobile_division_after_sale_talks_fall_through-news-48319.php|title = Report: LG considers shutting down mobile division after sale talks fall through}}</ref>

Other than mobile phones, LG Electronics have also made [[tablet computer]]s like the [[LG G series]] complementing the mobile phones.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.androidcentral.com/lg-unveils-trio-new-g-pad-tablets|title=LG G pad series|publisher=Android central|date=12 May 2014|access-date=7 July 2014}}</ref> LG also makes [[laptop computer]]s in the [[LG Gram]] line, and previously under the Xnote line (see [[List of LG laptops]]).

==== Mobile phones ====
{{See also|List of LG mobile phones}}
[[File:LG G4 Global Launching.jpg|thumb|right|200px|LG G4 range]]
LG Electronics used to manufacture mobile phones from 1995 to 2021,<ref name=":2">{{Cite news  |date=2021-04-05 |script-title=ko:초콜릿폰 성공에 너무 취했나…LG폰 철수의 결정적 이유 |url=https://news.mt.co.kr/mtview.php?no=2021040512562495445 |access-date=2023-07-16 |website={{ill|Money Today|ko|머니투데이}} |language=ko}}</ref> selling to the domestic market only (as [[LG Cyon|Cyon]]) until 2000 where it was in the shadow of [[Samsung Anycall]].<ref name=":2" /> LG released its first [[GSM]] network phones during 2001<ref>{{Cite web |title=LG — сетевое оборудование из Кореи! {{!}} КомпьютерПресс |url=https://compress.ru/article.aspx?id=10923%20https:/www.afaqs.com/news/advertising/2975_lg-calls-for-a-pitch |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=compress.ru |language=ru}}</ref> although had also marketed [[CDMA]] phones before then in the U.S.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CDMA Mobile Phones |url=http://www.lge.com/eng/product/e_ci/eng_ci_1.shtml |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=LG |archive-date=6 April 2001 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010406124527/http://www.lge.com/eng/product/e_ci/eng_ci_1.shtml |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref> LG made its breakthrough during the mid and late 2000s: it launched its highly popular [[LG Chocolate]] in worldwide in 2006 which popularised touch-sensitivity. The following year it released the world's first capacitive touchscreen phone [[LG Prada]], and [[LG Shine|Shine]], cementing its focus on design:<ref name=":2" /> its phones during this era have led to LG being called alongside [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] as one of the pioneers of the rise of touchscreens.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nokia Tube, RIM Storm and LG Renoir: three new touchscreen big hitters |url=https://rethinkresearch.biz/articles/nokia-tube-rim-storm-and-lg-renoir-three-new-touchscreen-big-hitters/ |access-date=2023-07-16 |website=Rethink |language=en}}</ref> By 2008 LG had entered the top 3 worldwide leaders in mobile phones.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=기자) |first1=양종석 (전자신문 |date=2008-07-15 |script-title=ko:'치고 받고' 절대 강자 없네 |url=https://www.sisajournal.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=123707 |access-date=2023-07-16 |website=[[Sisa Journal]] |language=ko}}</ref>

There was further success with the [[LG Cookie (KP500)|Cookie]] which helped to bring touchscreens to the budget market, and with the Lollipop flip phone that became very popular in South Korea.<ref name=":2" /> However the company had trouble with competing in smartphones. In 2010, LG released the [[LG Optimus (original)|Optimus]] smartphone, which would span into a series. The following year saw the release of the [[LG Optimus 3D]], the world's first mobile phone with glasses-free 3D display,<ref>{{Cite web |author1=Gary Cutlack |date=2011-07-06 |title=LG Optimus 3D review |url=https://www.techradar.com/reviews/phones/mobile-phones/lg-optimus-3d-930902/review |access-date=2023-07-16 |website=TechRadar |language=en}}</ref> and [[LG Optimus 2X]], the first with a dual-core processor.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2021-04-12 |title=LG mobile phone song finally exits: goodbye my "chocolate" |url=https://iphonewired.com/industry/105179/ |access-date=2023-07-16 |website=iPhone Wired |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2012 LG worked with [[Google]] to build the [[Nexus 4]] smartphone.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-14 |title=Happy birthday: The Google Nexus 4 is 10 years old |url=https://www.androidpolice.com/google-nexus-4-turns-10-retrospective/ |access-date=2023-07-16 |website=Android Police |language=en}}</ref>

Other than the [[LG G3|G3]], LG officially unveiled the curved smartphone, [[LG G Flex]], on 27 October 2013.<ref name="engadget-gflexfcc">{{Cite web|url=https://www.engadget.com/2013/11/15/lg-g-flex-att-lte/|title=LG G Flex appears on the FCC with AT&T-friendly LTE|website=www.engadget.com|date=15 November 2013 |access-date=9 March 2014}}</ref><ref name="engadget-gflexannounce">{{Cite web|url=https://www.engadget.com/2013/10/27/lg-g-flex/|title=LG G Flex announced with vertically curved 6-inch 720p screen, 'self-repairing' back cover|website=www.engadget.com|date=28 October 2013 |access-date=9 March 2014}}</ref> At [[Consumer Electronics Show]] in January 2014, LG announced a US release for the [[LG G2|G2]] across several major carriers.<ref name="verge-gflex-usa">{{Cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2014/1/6/5279814/lg-g-flex-launching-att-sprint-t-mobile|title=LG G Flex coming to AT&T, Sprint, and T-Mobile this winter|work=The Verge|date=6 January 2014|access-date=9 March 2014}}</ref> In 2015, LG released [[LG G4]] globally in late May through early June.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cnet.com/products/lg-g4/|title=G4 release date|publisher=CNET|access-date=6 May 2015}}</ref> On 7 September 2016, LG unveiled the [[LG V20|V20]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mobigyaan.com/lg-v20-unveiled|title=LG V20 unveiled with Android 7.0 Nougat, dual rear cameras and secondary screen|website=MobiGyaan.com|date=7 September 2016|access-date=7 September 2016}}</ref> and the [[LG V30|V30]] was announced on 31 August 2017. [[LG G6]] was officially announced during [[Mobile World Congress|MWC 2017]] on 26 February 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.androidauthority.com/lg-g6-release-date-price-specs-features-738704/|title=LG G6 officially announced: everything you need to know|date=26 February 2017}}</ref> The G7 ThinQ model was announced at a 2 May 2018 media briefing.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.eweek.com/mobile/lg-confirms-media-briefing-to-introduce-g7-thinq-android-smartphone|title=LG Confirms Media Briefing to Introduce G7 ThinQ Android Smartphone|last=Reisinger|first=Don|work=eWeek|date=11 April 2018|access-date=14 April 2018|department=Mobile}}</ref> In 2020, the [[LG Wing]] was introduced with two displays and a swivel design.<ref name=":4" />

In April 2021, after months of speculation, LG confirmed that the smartphone division will be officially shut down in July 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-04-05|title=LG to pull out of mobile phone market|url=http://www.theguardian.com/technology/2021/apr/05/lg-to-pull-out-of-mobile-phone-market|access-date=2021-04-12|website=the Guardian|language=en}}</ref> The decision to shut down LG Mobile came about from poor sales caused by stiff competition from rival Samsung and Chinese brands such as [[Oppo]] and [[Xiaomi]]. LG became the first major smartphone brand to completely withdraw from the market.<ref>{{cite news

===== Smart watches =====
[[File:LG G Watch R (2).jpg|thumb|200px|LG G Watch R]]
LG and Google announced the [[Android Wear]]-based [[smartwatch]], the [[LG G Watch]], that was in June 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.androidauthority.com/android-wear-io-official-397096/|title=Android Wear platform fully unveiled at I/O 2014|date=25 June 2014|publisher=Android Authority|access-date=25 June 2014|archive-date=23 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150323025103/http://www.androidauthority.com/android-wear-io-official-397096/}}</ref> In August 2014, the [[LG G Watch R]] that has a circular face (similar to the [[Moto 360]]) was released.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/lg-g-watch-r-photo-2014-8|title=This Is LG's New Round-Face Smartwatch: The G Watch R|work=Business Insider|access-date=27 August 2014}}</ref> The [[LG Watch Urbane]] that LG's third Android Wear-based smart watch has released in April 2015. This was the first device to support newer smartwatch features such as [[Wi-Fi]], and new parts of [[Android Wear]]'s software interface, like the ability to draw emoji to friends.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cnet.com/products/lg-watch-urbane/|title=LG Watch Urbane review|publisher=CNET|access-date=12 May 2015}}</ref>

===== Rolly keyboard =====
In 2015, LG announced a [[Bluetooth]] keyboard that folds up along the four rows of keys for portability. The Rolly keyboard is made of solid plastic. Two tiny plastic arms fold out from the end of the [[Keyboard (computing)|keyboard]] to support a [[Tablet computer|tablet]] or [[smartphone]] and it can toggle between two different Bluetooth-connected devices at a time. Battery life is an expected three months on a single AAA battery.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2015/8/27/9213551/lg-rolly-keyboard-announced|title=LG's new Rolly wireless keyboard turns into a pocket stick|work=The Verge|date=27 August 2015|access-date=27 August 2015}}</ref>

== Competitive position: innovation ==
In 2021, the [[World Intellectual Property Organization|World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)]]'s annual [[World Intellectual Property Indicators]] report ranked LG's number of patent applications published under the [[Patent Cooperation Treaty|PCT System]] as 4th in the world, with 2,759 patent applications being published during 2020.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=World Intellectual Property Indicators 2021|url=https://www.wipo.int/edocs/pubdocs/en/wipo_pub_941_2021.pdf|access-date=30 November 2021|website=WIPO}}</ref> This position is an impressive increase from its previous ranking as 10th in 2019 with 1,646 applications.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|author1=World Intellectual Property Organization|url=https://www.wipo.int/publications/en/details.jsp?id=4526|title=World Intellectual Property Indicators 2020|publisher=World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)|year=2020|isbn=978-92-805-3201-2|series=World IP Indicators (WIPI)|doi=10.34667/tind.42184|access-date=2021-08-26}}</ref>

In 2023, the [[World Intellectual Property Organization|World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)]]'s Annual PCT Review ranked LG Electronics's number of patent applications published under the [[Patent Cooperation Treaty|PCT System]] as 6th in the world, with 1,887 [[patent application]]s being published during 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=PCT Yearly Review 2024 |url=https://www.wipo.int/edocs/pubdocs/en/wipo-pub-901-2024-en-patent-cooperation-treaty-yearly-review-2024.pdf |page=39|access-date=2026-08-10}}</ref>

In 2024 LG's number of designs in [[industrial design]] registrations published under the [[Hague Agreement Concerning the International Deposit of Industrial Designs|Hague System]] was ranked as 4th in the world, with 352 design registrations being published during 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hague Yearly Review 2024 |url=https://www.wipo.int/edocs/pubdocs/en/wipo-pub-930-2024-en-hague-yearly-review-2024.pdf |website=wipo.int|access-date=2026-08-10}}</ref>

==Marketing and public relations==

===Sponsorships===

LG Sports Limited, a subsidiary of LG Corporation, owns the [[Korean Baseball Organisation]] (KBO) [[LG Twins]] (LG 트윈스). Through an acquisition in 1990, the [[Munhwa Broadcasting Corporation|MBC]] Blue Dragons (who was one of the six original founding members of the KBO in 1982) became the LG Twins.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapId=37257025|title=Company Overview of LG Sports Ltd.|work=[[Bloomberg News|Bloomberg]]|access-date=30 April 2019}}</ref> The team has won two Korean Series (1990 and 1994). LG attracts a large attendance of fans and to much of their enjoyment, took third place in the league.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://korea.stripes.com/travel/korean-pro-baseball-league-hit-fans|title=Korean pro baseball league a hit with fans|work=[[Stars and Stripes (newspaper)|Stars and Stripes]]|date=28 April 2014|access-date=30 April 2019|archive-date=16 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200916165031/https://korea.stripes.com/travel/korean-pro-baseball-league-hit-fans}}</ref>

In August 2013, LG Electronics announced that it would sponsor German [[Bundesliga]] club [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen]] for the next three years with an option to extend for one more year. LG sponsors the [[International Cricket Council]], the world governing body for [[cricket]] and also sponsors the [[ICC Awards]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://icc-cricket.yahoo.net/the-icc/about_the_organisation/partners.php|title=Commercial Partners of the International Cricket Council (ICC)|publisher=icc-cricket.yahoo.net|access-date=26 September 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090825143451/http://icc-cricket.yahoo.net/the-icc/about_the_organisation/partners.php|archive-date=25 August 2009}}</ref>

From 2009 to 2013, LG Electronics sponsored [[Formula One]] as a Global Partner and Technology Partner.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/news/headlines/2008/11/8739.html|title=The Official Formula 1 Website|publisher=Formula One|date=26 November 2008|access-date=10 June 2009}}</ref> LG was also an official supplier to Virgin Racing and Lotus Racing team, plus engine manufacturer Cosworth from 2010 to 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://hotcellularphone.com/lg/lg-extends-formula-1-reach-virgin-racing/|title=Welcome hotcellularphone.com|work=hotcellularphone.com|access-date=2026-08-10}}</ref> LG also sponsors London Fashion Week and the LG Arena in Birmingham.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.prlog.org/10129577-londons-first-ever-snow-and-music-festival-strengthens-lgs-corporate-sponsorship-portfolio.html|title=London's first ever snow and music festival strengthens LG's corporate sponsorship portfolio|publisher=Prlog.org|access-date=10 June 2009}}</ref>

During the period 2001–2003, LG sponsored the snooker [[Grand Prix (snooker)|Grand Prix]]. During these years the tournament was known as the ''LG Cup''. In 2008, LG became sponsors of the Extreme Sport 'FSO4 Freeze' festival.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.londonfreeze.com/index.php|title=FSO4 Freeze, Sponsored by LG, Snowboard and Music Festival|publisher=Londonfreeze.com|access-date=10 June 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080916170651/http://www.londonfreeze.com/index.php|archive-date=16 September 2008}}</ref>

The LG Electronics company in Australia dissolved its sponsorship with cricketer [[David Warner (cricketer)|David Warner]] on 27 March 2018 and dropped him as the brand ambassador of the company over the [[Australian cricket team in South Africa in 2017–18#Ball tampering|ball tampering scandal]] during the [[Australian cricket team in South Africa in 2017–18#3rd Test|third Test]] of their [[Australian cricket team in South Africa in 2017–18|2017–18 tempestuous series against South Africa]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2018/mar/28/electronics-giant-lg-drops-david-warner-as-brand-ambassador|title=Electronics giant LG drops David Warner as brand ambassador|agency=Australian Associated Press|website=[[The Guardian]]|date=28 March 2018|access-date=28 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.scmp.com/sport/other-sport/article/2139269/lg-drops-sponsorship-disgraced-david-warner-amid-australia-cricket|title=LG drops sponsorship of disgraced Aussie cricketer Warner|work=South China Morning Post|access-date=28 March 2018}}</ref> Warner had an agreement with the company in 2014 and his contract had been planned for renewal.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://scroll.in/field/873579/lg-electronics-decides-to-not-renew-contract-with-david-warner-after-ball-tampering-scandal|title=LG Electronics decides to not renew contract with David Warner after ball-tampering scandal|work=Scroll.in|access-date=28 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.smh.com.au/business/companies/lg-decides-not-to-renew-david-warner-sponsorship-20180328-p4z6pj.html|title=LG decides 'not to renew' David Warner sponsorship|last=Gray|first=Darren|website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]|date=28 March 2018|access-date=28 March 2018}}</ref>

==Controversies==
In 2010, independent tests of popular LG fridge models conducted by [[Choice (Australian consumer organisation)#CHOICE (Australian magazine)|Choice magazine]] found the energy consumption in two models was higher than claimed by LG. LG was aware of the problem and offered compensation to affected customers.<ref name="choicelg">{{Cite web|url=http://www.choice.com.au/Life-Stage/Green-living/Green%20products%20and%20appliances/LG-greenwash/page/Uncool%20claims.aspx|title=Choice exposes false energy claims by major fridge manufacturer, LG, for its GC-L197NFS|publisher=Choice|access-date=27 October 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101125162115/http://www.choice.com.au/life-stage/green-living/green%20products%20and%20appliances/lg-greenwash/page/uncool%20claims.aspx|archive-date=25 November 2010}}</ref> In 2004, LG made 4A-rated water efficiency claims for numerous washing machines before they were certified. LG gave undertakings to the [[Australian Competition & Consumer Commission]] to provide appropriate corrective notices and upgrade and maintain its trade practices compliance program. In 2006, LG overstated energy efficiency on five of its air conditioner models and was again required to offer consumers rebates to cover the extra energy costs.<ref name="choicelg"/>

In 2026, LG's [[end-user license agreement]] for their smart TVs included a notice that the device may record and analyze voices for its AI-based features. To comply with [[Wiretapping#Legal status|wiretapping laws]], it requests users to notify their household members and guests that the device may be recording voices.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Marshall |first1=Carrie |title='Pretty revolting': LG's TV and gaming monitors are getting huge backlash from users due to reportedly installing PC software without asking you, and insisting that you get consent from your guests so your TV may record their conversations |url=https://www.techradar.com/televisions/lgs-gaming-monitors-and-tvs-are-facing-a-user-revolt |website=[[TechRadar]] |language=en |date=17 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Terms and Conditions of Use {{!}} LG Electronics US |url=https://www.lg.com/us/legal |website=LG USA | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260910004225/https://www.lg.com/us/legal |archive-date=2026-09-10}}</ref> Furthermore, it was discovered by YouTube channel Gamers Nexus that some LG smart TVs may be recording and processing background audio and scan for other devices on [[Local area network|LAN]] even when in standby mode or disconnected from the internet.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Preston |first1=Dominic |title=LG TVs caught spying even when offline or on standby |url=https://www.theverge.com/tech/991190/lg-tv-spying-standby-recording-wi-fi-scanning-gamers-nexus |website=[[The Verge]] |date=8 September 2026}}</ref> However, LG denied such claims in response, claiming that they only process audio when a wake word of a voice command is detected, and that its ability to scan for other devices on the network is "a standard function commonly available on smart TVs and smart home devices".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Marshall |first1=Carrie |title='We know who's in the LG household… we own the glass': A new report says LG TVs gather way more personal data than we feared — but LG says the claims 'are not true' |url=https://www.techradar.com/televisions/lg-tvs-collect-far-more-data-on-you-than-youd-expect-says-new-report-including-logging-microphone-audio-while-on-standby |website=TechRadar |language=en |date=7 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Joseph |first1=Jibin |title=LG Denies Claims That Its TVs Eavesdrop on Users Even When the Screen Is Off |url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/lg-denies-tvs-eavesdrop-on-users-even-when-screen-is-off |website=PCMAG |language=en |date=10 September 2026}}</ref>

WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: Major appliance
======================================================================

{{Short description|Large machine which accomplishes routine housekeeping}}
{{broader|Home appliance}}

[[File:HK Central 豐澤電器 Fortress shop 萬邦行 Melbourne Plaza March 2019 SSG 03.jpg|thumb|A selection of major appliances at [[AS Watson|Fortress department store]] at [[Queen's Road, Hong Kong|Melbourne Plaza]], Hong Kong in March 2019]]

A '''major appliance''' is a non-portable or semi-portable [[machine]] used for routine [[housekeeping]] tasks such as [[cooking]], washing [[laundry]], or [[food preservation]]. Such appliances are sometimes collectively known as '''white goods''', as the products were traditionally white in color, although a variety of colors are now available. An appliance is different from a [[plumbing fixture]] because it uses [[electricity]] or [[fuel]].

Major appliances differ from [[small appliance]]s because they are bigger and not portable. They are often considered [[Fixture (property law)|fixture]]s and part of [[real estate]] and as such they are often supplied to tenants as part of otherwise unfurnished rental properties. Major appliances may have special electrical connections, connections to gas supplies, or special plumbing and ventilation arrangements that may be permanently connected to the appliance. This limits where they can be placed in a home.

Since major appliances in a home consume a significant amount of energy, they have become the objectives of programs to improve their [[Efficient energy use|energy efficiency]] in many countries. Increasing energy efficiency is often described as an important element of [[climate change mitigation]] alongside other improvements like [[Retrofitting|retrofitting buildings]] to increase [[building performance]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-02-06 |title=Building Retrofitting |url=https://drawdown.org/solutions/building-retrofitting |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209003500/https://drawdown.org/solutions/building-retrofitting |archive-date=2021-02-09 |access-date=2021-02-27 |website=Project Drawdown |language=en}}</ref> Energy efficiency improvements may require changes in construction of the appliances, or improved control systems. Starting in the 1990s major appliances such as washing machines and air conditioners started to incorporate fuzzy logic-based controls, replacing electromechanical controls such as wash timers in washing machines. These controls incorporated microcontrollers and sensors to control appliance operation at reduced cost while allowing the microcontroller to adjust appliance operation in real time without human intervention, resulting in improved appliance performance.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Sensors, appliance control, and fuzzy logic {{!}} IEEE Journals & Magazine {{!}} IEEE Xplore | url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/287530 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240519012710/https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/287530 | access-date=2026-08-19 | archive-date=2024-05-19}}</ref>

==Terminology ==
They are also known as a '''large domestic appliance''' or '''large electric appliance''' or simply a '''large appliance''', '''large domestic''', or '''large electric'''.

==Brands==
[[File:Cosmo Appliances Gas Range.jpg|thumb|A modern gas [[stove]]]]
In the early days of [[electrification]], many major consumer appliances were made by the same companies that made the generation and distribution equipment.{{cn|date=October 2016}} While some of these brand names persist to the present day, even if only as licensed use of old popular brand names, today many major appliances are manufactured by companies or divisions of companies that specialize in particular appliances.

==Types==
[[File:LGwashingmachine.jpg|thumb|A modern front-loading [[washing machine]]]]
[[Image:Drying cupboard 002.JPG|thumb|A [[drying cabinet]]]]

Major appliances may be roughly divided as follows:
*[[Refrigeration]] equipment
**[[Freezer]]
**[[Refrigerator]]
**[[Water cooler]]
**[[Ice maker]]
*[[Cooking]]
**[[Kitchen stove]], also known as a range, cooker, oven, cooking plate, or cooktop
**[[Wall oven]]
*[[Washing]] and [[drying]] equipment
**[[Washing machine]]
**[[Clothes dryer]]
**[[Drying cabinet]]
**[[Dishwasher]]
*Heating and cooling
**[[Air conditioner]]
**[[Furnace (house heating)|Furnace]]
**[[Water heating|Water heater]]
**[[Central heating|Central heating system]]
